Russell: [――. Let us hear it.]

Subaru: [From here on out, I’d like to go with strategies that, well, cause as little harm to others as possible. ――Is that no good?]

Russell slightly widened his eyes at that plea, and behind him, Black Dog laughed a “Kuha”.

He was aware that he was saying something unreasonable. But, as a matter of fact, nobody had died during the incident on this occasion. It would be difficult when it came to dealing with those whom Capella had gotten her hands on, but they should still be able to oppose that to the very end.

As Subaru thought so, before Russell could even say anything――,

White Sheep: [M-me too! I also think… that Subaru-san’s way of doing things, is good…]

Crusch: [There is nothing more ideal than concluding things with minimal casualties. Of course, I believe that we ought to follow a certain order of priority in order to get things done, but… lives rank quite highly in my personal order of precedence.]

White Sheep and Crusch were in agreement with Subaru’s opinion, and there was also no way that Ferris would object. Black Dog’s sneer went without saying, but surprisingly, Rachins snorted his nose but did not repudiate it.

And, as a matter of course, Subaru’s like-minded best partner was――,

Beatrice: [Of course, Betty’s view is the same as Subaru’s, in fact. After all, Subaru has always silenced everyone by recklessly doing the impossible, I suppose. This time shall be no different, in fact.]

Subaru: [You’re sorta making me sound like a terrible troublemaker , but, thank you.]

Articulating so with a smile, Subaru hugged Beatrice by his lap, and plumped himself down into his seat. He was to the left of Ferris, who had sat down before him. Then, on his other side, Crusch took her seat.

Sandwiching Subaru and Beatrice, Crusch and Ferris had aligned themselves to his sides.

Subaru: [Shit. I picked the wrong seat. Um, I guess I’ll just move…]

Ferris: [Hey, Subaru-kun. Could you pass a message to the person by your side? “That strange power might place an unexpected burden on your body, so it would be best not to overrely on it~”, kay?]

Subaru: [No, err…]

Crusch: [Natsuki Subaru, pass the following message onto the individual by your side. “It is likely that I will once more fall asleep for a short while. If you are concerned regarding my body, you are free to inspect it whilst I am slumbering”, that is all.]

Subaru: [Come on, does that really need to go through me!? Let’s all just speak honestly! Both of you seem like you can talk!]

However, neither Ferris, who rested his chin in his hands as he looked to the day after tomorrow, nor Crusch, who shut her eyes as she folded her arms, were willing to lend an ear to Subaru’s cries.

Although it was extremely reassuring and joyous that Crusch and Ferris were both part of the promising ensemble to save this Kingdom, the pattern of their relationship was not yet ready to openly express their gratitude.

Subaru: [The road ahead… the road ahead will be fraught with difficulties.]

As he slumped his shoulders, crestfallen, he placed his chin on the head of Beatrice in his lap. While Beatrice felt that weight, she began to pat Subaru’s head from below without reservation.

――The battle to save Emilia, to save his comrades carving their own path, and to save the Kingdom of Lugunica all in one go, commenced. A battle that would surely be no less rigorous than any that had come before.

Indeed, in the background of that strong resolve and determination donned by Natsuki Subaru, while gazing out at the shrinking sight of the Royal Capital,

Russell: [You hadn’t written about anything of this sort in your letters, Roswaal. Did you not provide the necessary Knightly training to ensure Emilia-sama would prevail, as per your desires…?]

Thus grumbled the man of the intelligence agency forced to deal with a responsibility outside the scope of his calculations, utterly stunned as he was.

--- Chapter 25: With Love, I Long To See You Smile Again ---

――He had imagined that the time to pay off his accrued debts would have arrived more dramatically.

???: [――Heinkel Astrea-dono, there is an active order requiring your presence at the Royal Capital. You shall be coming with us.]

Informed as such by the Knights that surrounded him, all clad in the white garb of the Kingdom’s Royal Guard, Heinkel had been sitting in the corner of a tavern during the middle of the day, cheap booze in hand, anguishing over the gloominess of his future prospects.

Faced with the Knights who, aware of his identity, had called for his surrender, Heinkel felt genuine sympathy for them, seeing as how they were being forced to do a job they did not want to do.

Heinkel: [Royal Capital, the Royal Capital, huh… just what crime could they possibly be trying to arrest me for?]

Knight: [Unfortunately, we lack the authorization to inform you. Still, if you are going to resist…]

The air of tension amongst the knights rose palpably.

His exhales carried a thick scent of liquor, but the intoxication had yet to reach his head. Through the senses of his skin, Heinkel deduced that other than the three before his eyes, there was also a squadron of Knights waiting outside the tavern.

To make a long story short, they would not hesitate to use force. And, Heinkel did not possess the strength to force their senses of duty to yield.

Above all――,

Heinkel: [Even if I flee, it’s a stalemate, huh…]

It was not at all as though he had merely been gulping down cheap booze in despair. Before he ever filled his mouth with liquor, he had thoroughly wracked his mind in search of any means possible. After that, the reason he had headed to this tavern was because no matter how far he went, he had not wished to admit it. ――That he had already exhausted every possible option.

Heinkel: [――――]

Looking down at the cup still half filled with alcohol atop the bar counter, Heinkel bit his lip.

For the two objectives Heinkel needed to accomplish no matter what, there was a position he absolutely needed to acquire at any cost―― a position that would allow him to intervene in the Royal Selection.

Originally, his contact with Priscilla had been a coincidence, so it was purely by chance that he had been granted that position, but he had realized far too late that it was something he could not afford to lose. Hence, the best course of action Heinkel could take would be to seek employment at one of the two camps that remained after excluding the Crush Camp, where his father was involved, and the Felt Camp, where his son was involved.

Heinkel: [Emilia-sama’s camp is out of the question, and the Kararagi… Anastasia-sama’s camp would also probably be…]

Unfeasable; even Heinkel could comprehend that.

He would have liked to place hope in Anastasia’s reasonability as a merchant, but as he had learned in the Vollachian Empire, she was quite friendly with Emilia. In all likelihood, she would have already heard about the disgraceful display Heinkel had made in front of Emilia.

Even if not, Heinkel was also self-aware that his reputation was the absolute worst.

Ergo, Heinkel had no chance of being employed by any of the Royal Candidates.

And thus, that had been more than enough of a reason for him to have been completely crushed, the faint ray of hope he had begun to glimpse extinguished.

Knight: [Heinkel Astrea-dono. ――Your response.]

Pressed for a definitive answer amidst the mounting tension, Heinkel gulped down all the remaining booze in his cup, and lowered his hands.

Not once did he feel the mettle to attempt reaching for the beloved sword by his waist.

As they escorted him away, they did not even bother binding Heinkel’s arms as they stuffed him in a dragon carriage, somewhat anticlimactically.

He had been fully prepared for a more violent journey, such that they did not even treat him as human.

Heinkel: […In the end, what sort of pretext is this?]

Stuck between the Knights who, as always, would not answer him even if he asked, Heinkel pondered what crime of his was being called into question. ――There were many possibilities that came to mind.

He had completely abandoned both his obligations as Deputy Commander of the Royal Guard, and his position as lord of the Astrea domain; it was also completely possible that he was under suspicion of meddling in the domestic affairs of the Vollachian Empire. If it was about something more recent, there was also the fact that he had been about to assist in the scheme plotted by Aldebaran.

But then again, as he was the one who had been approached with the proposal, he wished to cry out, “This isn’t what we agreed on!” seeing as the plan had completely fallen apart before even a single thing could commence.

However, Heinkel did not have any intent of blaming Aldebaran for that.

Someone had attempted to accomplish something, and it had come to an end with them having failed to achieve it. If that were something to be blamed for, then even if Heinkel were to drown to death a hundred times in a sea of blame, it would still not be enough.

Once again, everything was back to square one.

That went for both dragging Reinhard down from the seat of Sword Saint, and awakening his wife who had been slumbering for nigh on twenty years.

Or, perhaps this was a good time.

With even his reason to keep struggling on taken away from him, perhaps this was a good time for him to be told to just give up already. If that were the case, he might have even laughed.

Heinkel: […Still, this is strange.]

Escorted all the way to the Royal Capital by the Knights who had assiduously refused to tell him anything over these few days, Heinkel furrowed his brow at the fact that he had not come out of the dragon carriage to the sight of the Royal Castle, a guard station, or even a prison.

What lay before his eyes was an old chapel constructed in a section of the Royal Capital―― belonging to the Church of the Divine Dragon, it was a building that Heinkel found difficult to face directly.

Speaking of the Church of the Divine Dragon, it was the state religion of the Kingdom of Lugunica, a bastion of prayer where many citizens, though varying in their piety, devote their faith toward the Divine Dragon, whose favor they all partake in.

In the past, Heinkel too had ventured there many a time to offer up prayers, wishing for the awakening of his slumbering wife. ――But, after that night, never did he return. He had no right to set foot there; at present, that was Heinkel’s self-evaluation in regards to the church.

In the Church of the Divine Dragon’s house of prayer, what awaited Heinkel as he was shoved along through the entrance, was a girl in a nun’s habit, with long golden hair, and ruby eyes――,

???: [Ah! I’ve been waiting for you, Heinkel-sama!]

The instant she saw Heinkel’s face, the girl clamorously flew out of her chair, quickly rushing toward him. At the momentum of the restless girl wearing a beaming smile, Heinkel reflexively took half a step back.

What he had sensed was not hostility. It was goodwill. The reason he had fallen back was not because of a threat. It was because of suspicion. The reason for that suspicion, upon eyeing the girl up and down once more, immediately connected.

Beautiful golden hair, and ruby eyes akin to blazing jewels.

Those traits ought to have been impossible.

Girl: [――I am Filóre Lugunica. I’m delighted to have the pleasure of meeting you like this, Heinkel-sama. I’ve been looking forward to your arrival!]

Heinkel: [ Fil… oh-re…!? ]

Filóre: [――? Yes, that is correct, Filóre. That is my… wait, that’s right! People who know it are always shocked when they hear it! Recently, everything all around me has gotten all busy and hectic, so I forgot to be careful about that.]

Sticking out her tongue to hide her embarrassment as she spoke, as the girl―― as the one who called herself Filóre faced him, Heinkel could not put into words the turbulence that had assailed him.

After all, it was impossible for there to be two people in this world who bore that name.

Filóre: [All of you, thank you very much for your assistance. For your wonderful work, the Dragon will also surely be delighted. “The arm of man doth swing the sword, but it be the Dragon’s will that deals in life. Under the footprints of a Knight chosen, even the most bloodied of ruts turn to roads of silver.” This too, is in the scriptures.]

Filóre called out to the Knights standing at the entrance to the chapel, behind the shaken Heinkel. At the sonorous reverberation of her voice, the Knights all exchanged glances.

Of course, from their perspective, having been the ones to drag Heinkel here, they would not want to do something like leaving Filóre and Heinkel alone here. But, without taking notice of the Knights’ concerns, Filóre declared “You need not fear!” with a clenched fist,

Filóre: [This personage is of the line of Sword Saints, the magnificent gentleman chosen by the Divine Dragon, I give him my personal stamp of approval! This is an extremely momentous encounter for the very Kingdom itself!]

As Filóre thud her own chest and talked bombastically, the Knights’ discomfiture did not fade.

On the other hand, Heinkel also had some vehement reservations about her remarks. It was to such an extent that it had managed to pull him back to reality from the initial shock of her name.

Knight: [If anything happens, please call out. We shall be on standby outside.]

Given their position, that was the limit on how much they were able to compromise.

And leaving those words behind, keeping a stern gaze on Heinkel until the very end, the Knights closed the entrance to the chapel, and took their posts outside. Once the sight of those Knights disappeared behind the doors, Filóre grumbled “How difficult” whilst folding her arms.

Filóre: [The situation is what it is, so it’s only natural that everyone is so worried, but… right now, this takes priority. Once again, Heinkel Astrea-sama, it is a pleasure to…]

Heinkel: [――Just before, what the hell were you trying to do?]

Filóre: [ Fweh ?]

Taking a step, he closed the distance of the half-step he had previously taken back, and questioned the other party. In doing so, as he looked down at Filóre from up close, her ruby eyes widened.

What discomforting eyes those were. In her refined facial features, he sensed far too many similarities to the Lugunican Royal Family. ――But, that could not be possible.

Heinkel: [Filóre Lugunica, is the princess who vanished from the castle fifteen years ago. And if it’s about her, she was already found in the slums quite a while ago, and now, in the Royal Selection…]

Filóre: [――Ah, you mean Felt, right? Indeed, I’ve heard that she also has those suspicions hanging over her. But, amongst ourselves, we have reached the conclusion that it doesn’t matter either way.]

Heinkel: [Ah…?]

Filóre: [It is possible that either she or myself is that princess who disappeared from the Royal Castle fifteen years ago. As it so happens, both of us are around fifteen years of age, and I believe there is a miraculous serendipity transpiring in that regard. However, that is unimportant.]

Heinkel: [J-just what sort of ridiculous nonsense are you on about!]

As Filóre brazenly touched so nonchalantly upon one of the foremost incidents of the Kingdom, Heinkel raised his voice.

In reality, it was ridiculous nonsense. Due to that terrible incident, there were several things that had ended up straying from the right path. And, it was not a matter unrelated to Heinkel either.

On that night fifteen years prior, the several occurrences that took place at the Royal Castle Lugunica――,

Heinkel: [That ties back to what you said earlier! That I’m of the line of Sword Saints, that I was chosen by the Dragon, spouting all sorts of nonsense…]

Filóre: [But, fifteen years ago, the one who basked in the Dragon’s Blood kept safe in the Royal Castle, never succumbing to the power it holds, before ultimately adapting to it… wasn’t it you, Heinkel-sama?]

Heinkel: [Wha――]

Filóre: [Ah, this was something that needs to be kept secret, right? To tell you the truth, it was something I stealthily read in the confidential records of the Church, so I only realized later that it was something that couldn’t be spread around.]

Though Filóre was belatedly trying to keep her voice hushed, Heinkel was in no state to care about that.

The Dragon’s Blood from fifteen years prior; the fact that it was even brought up in the first place was a shock, but the pièce de résistance was the fact that it was documented in something like the confidential records of the Church of the Divine Dragon.

The reason was lost on him. There was certainly a time when Heinkel had frequented the church, but it was not as though he was a devout adherent, nor had he ever done anything like confessing his inner heart to no avail.

Above all――,

Heinkel: [――――]

The suspicions raised against him, and the events of that night fifteen years ago: he would absolutely never reveal them.

The responsibility for the matter did not lie with Heinkel alone. It was an incident of grave importance that could well impact the rest of House Astrea, and the entirety of the Kingdom of Lugunica.

It was by no means a matter that would be put to rest if Heinkel alone were to lay bare his own heart.

Heinkel: [Hah, I’ve got absolutely no idea what you’re going on about, you damn phony princess.]

Thus, as Heinkel’s cheeks contorted with spinelessness, he attempted to viciously scorn Filóre.

Upon hearing it, Filóre widened her eyes, catching her breath at Heinkel’s denial. Did she really not consider that she might be denied? In that case, she was a foolish girl.

Heinkel: [Did you think that if you crashed into things head-first with honesty, everything would just neatly bounce back to you? If so, that’s an unthinkably carefree approach. The world isn’t such a nice place.]

Filóre: [Heinkel-sama…]

Heinkel: [Don’t go slapping on honorifics as if they’re some kinda uniform! I don’t know what you’re expecting from me, but it’s too bad. Chosen by the Divine Dragon? Don’t joke with me. The line of Sword Saints? Is that your aim? The Royal Castle and the Church of the Divine Dragon have always kept a distance! If you guys revere the Divine Dragon above all else, then Reinhard must be in your way, yeah!?]

Rapidly spitting out a string of foul speech, he felt the depths of his chest being tainted in viscous black.

He had just been half-mindedly vocalizing his thoughts, but surprisingly, he felt like the words he was saying rang true. The name of the Sword Saint was renowned in the Kingdom of Lugunica, and in the current age of Reinhard, celebrated as the strongest one in history, it could possibly be said that it was approaching the realm of religious faith.

It was possible that for the Church of the Divine Dragon, Reinhard was something like a thorn in their side.

In order to remove that, it was completely conceivable that they intended to use Heinkel. ――That which, until now, Heinkel himself had used as a card in his negotiations with the Royal Candidates, was now tinged with an unpleasant clamminess.

But, perchance, considering one of Heinkel’s objectives, that could also――,

Filóre: [――The reason I sought you out, Heinkel-sama, is because I wanted to have you become my Knight.]

――.

――――.

――――――――.

Heinkel: […What?]

Due to his deep rumination, in which he ground his teeth to the point where he could taste blood, he felt like he had heard an odd auditory illusion.

If not that, it must have been some inexplicable mishearing ; Heinkel grimaced with such sentiments, however, paying no mind to his bafflement, Filóre raised her visage, and opened her mouth.

Once again, this time staring directly into his azure eyes,

Filóre: [Heinkel Astrea-sama, I wish for you to become my Knight. With a delayed entry into the Royal Selection, the Knight of this very Filóre Lugunica.]

Heinkel: [Idi…! A-are you insane…!?]

Filóre: [My, what an awful thing to say! I’ll warn you now, but if you swear an oath to serve me, I’d like for you to reform that attitude as much as possible.]

Forcing him to swallow the fact that he did not mishear her, she doubled down on the sentiment. But, no matter how many times she repeated it, there was no way a proper discussion could take place with such an unsteady foundation.

Filóre had said it. That as a Royal Candidate, she would have Heinkel be her one and only Knight.

Heinkel: [Who do you have whispering in your ear? Don’t tell me, was it Reinhard? Did he say something to you? Then…]

Filóre: [Don’t make jokes! How could I thoughtlessly make such an important decision based on what someone else tells me to do? I came to this decision completely by myself!]

Heinkel: [If that’s the case then you’ve really got no eye for this sort of thing whatsoever! Didn’t you tell anyone else? For example, those Knights out there. There ought to have been plenty of people you could have asked!]

Filóre: [Yes, I did ask them. Everyone made complicated faces, and insisted that I should rethink it.]

Heinkel: [Then listen and do as you’re told! Rethink it!]

Filóre: [I did rethink it! But, no matter how many times I rethink it, you always end up as my number one choice, Heinkel-sama.]

Placing her hands on her hips, Filóre puffed out her chest and answered proudly, leaving Heinkel speechless.

She was likely the type to stick with something to the end once she had decided on it. Even just judging from her behavior until now, he generally understood that. He understood it, but what the hell were the people around her doing?

Heinkel: [Miss Priscilla also had a stubborn side to her, never budging once she’d set her mind on something, but in her case, nobody could deny her decisiveness and ability to get things done…]

In the sense of not lending an ear to the words of those around them, it might have been a close contest.

But, between Priscilla and Filóre, there was a great disparity in their individual reliability, or rather, in the degree of their strength of character.

To put it bluntly, Priscilla had been an adult, and Filóre was a child. If a child was attempting to do something wrong, it was an adult’s duty to stop them.

Even if that child bore a prestigious title such as Royal Candidate, and even if the adult in the position to admonish them was a foolish, wretched failure who had no right to do so.

Heinkel: [Even if you’re a dreamer, that which you’re dreaming of right now is a nightmare. It’s the kind of bad dream where you won’t even lend an ear to everyone around you telling you it’s a nightmare. How could I possibly go along with that?]

As he asserted that, Heinkel derided his own foolish decision.

Even though he had lost any Royal Candidate to rely on, and had been drowning himself in alcohol without being able to achieve his desires, now that this hand, the best thing he could possibly have hoped for, had been extended to him like this, he did not grasp it back.

If it had truly been so important to him, he ought to have reached out his hand by any means, fair or foul. ――In that case, after having spent fifteen years, could it be that he was not really serious about it, still trying to pick and choose the hands he took?

All of it was naught more than the mere dregs of convictions firmly rooted within him, with Heinkel’s interior being completely empty――,

???: [――You’re spoolio! Heinkel-san!]

That instant, a voice clearly resonated in a corner of his mind, quaking Heinkel’s very soul.

Heinkel: [――Louanna.]

For nearly twenty years now, he had not heard her voice even a single time.

Even so, whenever he closed his eyes, and pictured her smile, he would be able to hear her voice not only as if it were just yesterday, but as if she was right there with him in this very moment. It was only natural. He loved her, after all.

Even if Heinkel was completely empty, he had been filled with an ardor known as Louanna, along with everything she had given him, and all of that was real.

Not once, not even for a single second, had any of that ever faded.

Filóre: [I am appointed as a Saintess of the Church of the Divine Dragon. The ideal I espouse as a Royal Candidate, starting with erasure of the ill feelings between the Royal Castle and the Church, is the complete abolition of any factors that stand in the way of bestowing salvation.]

Before the silent Heinkel, Filóre started speaking quietly, but with a certain strength in her voice.

Raising his visage, Heinkel gazed at Filóre. As always, she was staring directly toward Heinkel, however, the words she weaved were bereft of the same frivolous atmosphere from earlier.

In order to impart the words she had to share with him no matter what, she was carefully selecting her words, imbuing them with strength and sentiment alike; that much was clear to him.

Filóre: [Heinkel-sama, I’ve heard about your wife. It would seem as though you have been searching for a way to awaken her for over a decade, not once ever giving up. It is extremely admirable.]

Heinkel: […You think it’s admirable? I’ve accomplished nothing. Louanna still isn’t awake, so what the hell is…]

Filóre: [No, it’s admirable! Nobody has ever commended you for it, have they? But, I think it’s incredible! It’s not something that just anybody can do. You’re indomitable… no, I’m sure there have been times when your spirit has been broken. Even so, the fact that you were able to stand back up is amazing!]

Heinkel: [――――]

Filóre: [That’s the kind of person you are, which is why I want you to be my Knight. Of course, as a Saintess, I also can’t overlook the fact that you were chosen by the Dragon. But, you are someone who does everything in your power without ever giving up for the people precious to you. I’m sure we’ll make a great match!]

Raising her voice, Filóre extended her smooth, white hand. And as if imploring Heinkel to take her hand, her ruby eyes blazed as if a flame was alight within them.

A foolish girl; no matter how much he heard of what she had to say, that impression did not disappear.

The individual whom a Royal Candidate selected to be their one and only Knight would become an existence who they entrusted not only with their own life, but with their political destiny as well. Even with a lofty title like Saintess of the Church of the Divine Dragon, it was all prone to being blown away by Heinkel’s notoriety.

There was not even a sliver of a reason for Filóre to choose Heinkel as her Knight.

He would refuse her. He should refuse her. Not for anyone’s sake, but for the sake of this foolish girl before his eyes.

In order to prevent this foolish and gentle girl from being ridiculed as an idiot, from being insulted by everyone behind her back, Heinkel ought to refuse her request.

And even though he ought to have refused her――,

Heinkel: [――Let me hear… one thing.]

Even though he ought to have sneered at her, turned his back, and walked away, he ended up speaking those words.

It was not a refusal. Neither was it a disparagement. As he expressed intent to continue the conversation, Filóre inclined her head.

Filóre: [What is it?]

Heinkel: [I’ve heard that the Church of the Divine Dragon has secret arts of healing that are forbidden from being revealed to the public. Maybe… just maybe, if such a thing truly exists, then…]

Filóre: [――You mean the Sacrament?]

Heinkel: [――Hk! Is there really such a thing!?]

Filóre seemed to have an idea of what he was talking about, and Heinkel pounced at her words. ――That vigor of his caused Filóre to widen her eyes, before she cast her eyes slightly downward.

While the change in her expression affirmed the existence of the sacrament, it also told Heinkel that she was uncertain if it would meet his expectations―― if it would be useful in awakening his slumbering wife.

Filóre: [――. There is. But, I don’t know whether it will have an effect on your wife or not.]

Sure enough, after a moment of silence, Filóre shook her head from side to side.

But, he did not get overly dejected. Having his hopes dashed, and being pushed down to the bottom of the cliff was an experience Heinkel was by no means a stranger to. The fact that he would not die even when that happened, was a result he had verified many times.

Heinkel: [I see. Is that so… Ahh, that’s right.]

He had already experienced more than enough shame in his life.

If his mind was wired in any respectable way, then even his question just now was something he should not have asked. And yet, he had asked it. Upon doing so, his hopes were thrown to the wayside.

So now――,

Filóre: [――That’s why, we have no choice but to test it out. They’re always telling me that I mustn’t use it too frequently, but if it’s for the sake of helping people, it should be fine.]

Heinkel: [――Ah?]

Filóre: [Ah, but, as I said just now, I’m not certain if it will work. The Sacrament isn’t all powerful, and it also depends on the state of that person’s soul… however, the Church of the Divine Dragon also has a lot of other things that aren’t known to the public, so if we don’t give up, it should be possible to open a path forward. Yes, surely.]

Firmly clenching the hand opposite to her extended one into a fist, Filóre once more insisted the same way she had initially.

The contents of her insistence caused Heinkel to blink his eyes, and let out a ragged breath.

Heinkel: [――――]

Filóre did not say that it would work.

Neither did she say to leave it to her, nor promise that she would definitely save her. ――Merely, she vowed to not give up.

For nearly twenty years, Heinkel had failed to be understood by anyone, being ridiculed as a fool time and time again; the things he had never abandoned despite all that, were now being affirmed as completely natural by the girl before his eyes.

He knew. ――He knew that everyone, even the very Heinkel reflected in the mirror, constantly thought somewhere in the back of their minds that it might actually be impossible.

Filóre: [Heinkel-sama, please lead the way. No, House Astrea is indeed quite famous, so I also have a rough idea of where it is, but I feel hesitant about barging into a household when no family members are home. Moreover, it’s also a little complicated between me and Felt…]

As if to say that things could not remain like this, Filóre halted in her tracks after gallantly striding forward. Looking back toward Heinkel after passing him, she called out to usher him to accompany her.

And, having turned around, Filóre’s eyes widened in shock. ――After all, before her eyes, Heinkel was kneeling down where he had stood, and was bowing his head.

Filóre: [Heinkel, sama…?]

Heinkel: [I apologize for my repeated acts of discourtesy. Miss Filóre.]

Before the surprised Filóre, Heinkel deliberately refined his speech, and spoke.

Were he to become the Knight of a Royal Candidate, he would be involved in the Royal Selection once more.

If it were a Saintess who could wield even the sacrament kept hidden by the Church of the Divine Dragon, it might be possible to awaken Louanna.

If there was a chance she was the princess who carried the blood of the Royal Family, then with the authority she held, it might even be possible to obtain the ancient knowledge slumbering in the Royal Castle, or even the Dragon’s Blood itself.

If he enumerated such calculations, he could come up with any number of reasons to kneel.

But, the number one reason for why Heinkel knelt here, was not any of those calculations.

――Do I really still want to pretend to be a Knight, me of all people?

Heinkel: [I would like to accept your proposal. ――Allow me to be your Knight, Miss Filóre.]

Filóre: [――――]

Heinkel: [You may end up regretting that you chose me, but…]

Filóre: [No, I won’t! Never!]

As Filóre smiled like a flower in bloom, Heinkel looked a bit daunted, before biting down on the interior of his cheek.

Still kneeling, he unsheathed the sword at his waist, laid it on the ground, and performed a respectful bow. ――The way he straightened his back, the angle at which he looked up at his lady, and his knightly etiquette of dedicating his blade, none of it had been erased by his twenty years of disgrace.

The ruins of a Knight who had once pledged fealty to the Royal Family, now, after all this time, decided to put those airs on once more.

It was ridiculous. Truly, it was utterly ridiculous.

While completely daubed in that humorless ridiculousness, Heinkel Astrea became the one and only Knight to the brand new Royal Candidate, Filóre Lugunica.

――And those were the events of the day upon which Saintess and Backstabber established a relationship of master and servant.

--- Chapter 26: A Word of Congratulations ---

――From the very outset of when he had been appointed as Filóre’s Knight, Heinkel had felt a sense of impending crisis stemming from her headfirst personality, but that cognition of his had been incorrect.

Filóre’s recklessness had been far worse than Heinkel had ever imagined.

Filóre: [――So, you’re saying that even though the medicine is in the warehouse, it can’t be delivered?]

???: [Yes. The traffic of dragon carriages in and out of Royal Capital is far too congested, so the Church’s carts have all come to a standstill. At this rate…]

Filóre: [The medicine will go bad, and there are many elders at the treatment centers who will be in danger if they don’t take their medicine every day… if this is what it comes to, then we’ll just have to do our best to transport it with our own hands, how about it?]

???: [Eh!? W-with our own hands!?]

Filóre: [That’s right! If the dragon carriages can’t be moved, we’ll just have to carry out the cargo with human strength… don’t you think this could work!?]

At the entrance to the chapel of the Church of the Divine Dragon, a young man with a catalog of medicines in hand leaned a great deal backwards when met with Filóre’s vigor, the latter leaning towards him with her fists balled up.

Perhaps taking the young man’s reaction as an affirmation, Filóre seemed ready to rush over to the Commercial District at any moment, and so Heinkel hastened to keep her in check with a “Hold on, hold on”.

Heinkel: [Miss Filóre, if you take that approach, then the problem won’t be resolved even when the sun sets, and then rises again tomorrow. Don’t tell me you were seriously about to try carrying everything by yourself.]

Filóre: [What are you talking about, isn’t it obvious!? Heinkel-sama is my Knight, so we’re in the same boat, the same boat I tell you! I’m not going by myself, but with the two of us!]

Heinkel: [Like hell that’s going to happen! Even if say, for the sake of argument, we were to depend on manual labor, Miss Filóre, there’s no way I could let someone of your standing go. If anyone’s going, it’d be me on my own.]

Filóre: [Please don’t say such standoffish things. Believe it or not, I’m also quite strong myself. At the convent, I even used to help rearrange rooms all the time for the old ladies with poor backs!]

Heinkel: [That’s! Not! What I’m talking about!]

Filóre got carried away at full throttle, and her ruby eyes widened at Heinkel’s angry shout.

While she blinked her sparkling, gemstone-like eyes, Heinkel scratched at his own red hair, directing a displeased “Oi” to the young worker from the transport company.

Heinkel: [What’s needed is a way to transport the medicine to the treatment center in the eastern ward, yeah? There ought to also be treatment centers in the west and south, so what about those ones?]

Worker: [The western and southern ones? There are still viable routes to be taken there, so there is no risk of the medicine getting stuck along the way…]

Heinkel: [Then this will be a quick chat. Instead of the medicine, you should relocate the patients instead.]

As he spoke, Heinkel snatched the medicine catalog out from the hands of the young employee.

All the medicines listed there were ones he was familiar with, and he could also roughly imagine the conditions of the patients who were in need of them. ――Ever since his wife had fallen asleep, he had inquired into the remedies for every illness he could discover. Having made use of his privileged family status residing in the Royal Capital, Heinkel had a greater knowledge of medicine than the average healer.

Heinkel: [Although, it’s not like I’ve seen the patients for myself. Ultimately, the decision rests with the healers, but it’s more realistic than trying to figure out a way to get all the dragon carriages through, and if a route to the eastern ward can be secured while going through with the makeshift solution, everything should go smoothly from then on. ――Well, how’s that for now, Miss Filóre?]

Filóre: [Eh? Ehh! Yes! Ah, but, what about the people who can’t be moved from the treatment center…]

Heinkel: [It’s not like everyone in the treatment center is a severe case. Thus, as long as we pack a single crate with the most urgent medicines, it’ll last for the time being.]

Filóre: [I see! And as for that crate, I shall――]

Heinkel: [Oi…]

Filóre: [――Not do it, rather, I entrust it to you! After all, carrying things is your job!]

Pierced by Heinkel’s eyes, Filóre was discouraged, before turning a smile in the direction of the young worker. After he had gotten the catalog back from Heinkel, he nodded at Filóre’s words,

Worker: [Understood, I will act accordingly. As for the treatment centers…]

Filóre: [Please, rest assured. The treatment centers and the Church of the Divine Dragon are deeply involved with each other!  We will promptly send an envoy and act to ensure there are no misunderstandings. You may focus on your own duty.]

Worker: [――Yes! Both of you, thank you very much!]

Following an expression of relief, the young man bowed his head along with a sense of duty and left the chapel. After seeing him off, Heinkel slumped his shoulders in exhaustion.

From the very beginning to the end, Filóre had continued to give counsel without losing steam, so while it was fine for her to receive gratitude, it was a bit uncomfortable when the same was shown to Heinkel, who did nothing but remain by her side.

After all, he was a man who, truth be told, did not have any right to be standing here.

Filóre: [Hard work as always, Heinkel-sama! That was a discussion in which our brilliant coordination really got to shine, wasn’t it? Since we also sent out an envoy, he should be able to attend to his own duties with peace of mind.]

And, having no clue as to those inner feelings of Heinkel, Filóre returned after sending one of the Church’s adherents to go off as an envoy, before lightly holding her hand up to him. She did not bring it down. Even after staring at it for a while, she still did not bring it down, waving it left and right in front of Heinkel.

Heinkel: […What.]

Filóre: [Not “what”, it’s a ritual to extol our joint efforts. If I hoist my hand up like this, Heinkel-sama, then you also bring your hand up to meet it. By doing that, we get to share in the feeling of having guided each other well, it’s a custom in the Church of the Divine Dragon!]

Heinkel: [Back when I used to go to Church, I never saw anything like that.]

Filóre: [It might have been a recently added custom! And, it might have been slightly influenced by me!]

Considering the culture of the Church that had unchangingly worshiped the Divine Dragon for four hundred years, rather than new rituals coming in and out of fashion, the notion of Filóre having had a large influence was more convincing.

Unfortunately, it did not seem like Filóre would be satisfied until he completed the custom, so after another sigh, Heinkel clapped his own palm to her hand.

Heinkel: [Miss Filóre, about what you said earlier…]

Filóre: [Ah, that was some splendid tact! Rest assured. I also made sure to tell the envoy to inform the people at the treatment center that it was your idea, Heinkel-sama.]

Heinkel: [――. You need to have more self-restraint. And frankly, more self-respect too.]

Filóre: [Self-restraint!? I don’t like those words…!]

As if betrayed by her cheerful smile, Filóre turned pale as she staggered towards a bench within the chapel. While watching over her state, he let a deep exhale out of his nose.

He wished to avoid doubling the things he wanted to say in such a short period of time.

Heinkel: [To start things off, you need to stop plunging in head first, and taking actions akin to searching around in the ashes of a fireplace. You don’t know what’s going to be amidst the ashes, and in the majority of cases, you’re going to get burned. When you’ve got no other choice but to search through the ashes, make use of other people. Starting with me.]

Filóre: [That’s… because you’re an immortal Knight who can’t lose out to flames, Heinkel-sama?]

Heinkel: [Wrong. It’s because if anyone’s going to get hurt, it should be the people who don’t care about getting hurt.]

Deliberately stating those strict words clearly, he attempted to rectify Filóre’s thinking.

Filóre’s way of doing things was perilous. But, the ability to display a disposition that captivated people’s attention, was an indispensable quality for a politician. Given that she had gotten a delayed participation in the Royal Selection, she would need to, without metaphor, avoid the situations that were likely to burn her, and effectively play the cards in her hand.

That was why――,

Heinkel: [Don’t go bringing up my name each and every time. I’ll be blunt, but seriously, it will only get in the way of your campaign in the Royal Selection, Miss Filóre.]

Filóre: [No way…]

Heinkel: [But, because they heard it was my suggestion, the earlier matter with the treatment center might not go over so well. The fact that it wouldn’t be strange for such a thing to happen is the epitome of my current standing. Sorry, but I’m aware of it.]

Filóre: [――Hk.]

His answer appeared to frustrate Filóre, but since it was none other than himself who had caused her to make that face, Heinkel did not possess the words to comfort or encourage her.

To be perfectly honest, he was still regretting his decision. ――As expected, Heinkel should not have accepted the request of Filóre, which could only be seen as delusional.

Whenever he witnessed the attitude of his master, a girl who, while still clumsy, was earnestly taking part in the Royal Selection, more and more did he end up despising his own self, who served as naught but a hindrance to her ambitions.

Doubly so if when considering that all the infamy he had accrued until now had been earned through his own volition.

Heinkel: [In the end, nothing I do ever goes well…]

Even though on occasion, he would take action while aiming for the best path forward, after a bit of time, his past actions would creep up and wring him by the neck. Again and again, it was akin to as if Heinkel was running a few laps behind in his life, coming up on unavoidable traps that he had left behind. Tripping over the holes dug by his past self, he had lost count of how many times he had fallen over until now.

That was precisely why, whenever he was able to accomplish some sort of feat, it would be the best outcome for Filóre if the impurity known as Heinkel was not mixed in―,

Filóre: [――Enough, it’s not like me!]

And, narrowing her two eyes, Filóre suddenly shouted before Heinkel as he was deep in thought, and he noticed that she had been firmly pinching the back of her own white hand. Then, as she cried out “Owwwww!”, Heinkel widened his eyes.

Heinkel: [W-what are you doing?]

Filóre: [I’m admonishing my own fecklessness! In truth I would have liked to slap even just one of my cheeks, but if I did so I would need to go and meet people with a completely red face, right? So, since a long time ago, whenever I want to scold myself, I do this. If it’s just my hand that turns red, I can just make the excuse that I got so angry that I slammed the table!]

Heinkel: [Is that really a good excuse? I mean, it’d be clear that you got angry, but…]

Filóre: [It’s fine! After all, it’s the truth that I got angry! And also, regardless of what anyone tells me, this alone is something I won’t yield on. Going forward as well, I won’t hide Heinkel-sama’s contributions!]

As she firmly thrust her finger out at his face, Heinkel reflexively reeled backward. To close the distance which he had opened, Filóre took a step forward. Heinkel stepped back. She stepped forward. Stepped back. Stepped forward. Driving him up against the wall, she thrust her finger right against his forehead.

Then, as Filóre pressed Heinkel against the wall,

Filóre: [As for why everyone says all these bad things about you, Heinkel-sama, let’s say it’s because your behavior up until this point gives them a reason to do so. I find even that to be extremely frustrating, but I’ll swallow it for now. Even so! I can’t accept the notion that your actions from the past will dull the value of your actions today and tomorrow..]

Heinkel: [Miss Filóre…]

Filóre: [If there are lives that can be saved by your words, then if they didn’t have your words, their lives might not have been saved. If I’m going to be the Monarch, and you’re going to be my one and only Knight, then there are going to be many opportunities for you to be present at such scenes. Hence, in preparation for when such times inevitably come, Heinkel-sama, we must work to restore your honor at once!]

Heinkel: [――――]

Filóre: [And so, Heinkel-sama, I’ll listen to your advice as best I can, but I’ll never follow any comments that say I should just look down upon you, or that I should just hide you in a box, that I should just hurry up and throw away such an alcoholic of a Knight. I hereby declare this.]

Slowly lowering her finger, Filóre brought it down to feel the uniform adorning Heinkel―― his uniform as an official Knight of the Church, which he had been forced to wear given his position as Knight to a Saintess of the Church of the Divine Dragon.

With a base of blue, it was a sacred and sublime article, with the same amount, or an even greater number of layers in comparison to the uniforms of the Royal Guard, filling him with awe; it was an outfit he was fully aware did not suit him in the slightest.

However――,

Filóre: [But eventually, it will be so that when anyone so much as lays eyes upon these clothes, Heinkel-sama will be the first thing that comes to mind. When that time comes, it’ll be fine for you to make full use of the Church’s influence, and put on airs as much as you like.]

Shutting a single eye, Filóre made a clumsy display of amiability.

Harkening her words, Heinkel heaved a long sigh. That all-out, headfirst attitude of hers was something she applied to just about everyone. Of course, Heinkel was no exception.

Heinkel: […If Miss Filóre becomes the Monarch, huh? So, does that mean whenever you help others at the Church, it’s just a calculated act?]

Filóre: [Could you please not say such outrageous things!? You see, this is all an extremely good deal. By giving counsel to the people who come to the Church, they get help with their troubles, and I also build a reputation for doing good things, and it also feels nice for us when we do a good thing… right?]

Heinkel: [Don’t lump me in there as if it’s only natural. I’m…]

Filóre: [But, don’t you think it’s joyous to receive gratitude from others? That’s how it is for me. That’s why, even if the title of Saintess is heavy to shoulder, I quite like the Church.]

Puffing her chest out with a nod, Filóre’s words rendered Heinkel unable to respond.

Whether it was because Filóre had already said what she had wanted to say, or out of consideration for Heinkel, she did not press him for an answer.

Then, the chance for him to voice any answer, was postponed by the sound of the doors to the chapel opening once more.

???: [――Do you have a moment? There are some civilians getting into a fight right outside the Church.]

Filóre: [My, oh dear! We’ll rush there straight away! Heinkel-sama, us too!]

Heinkel: [――. Don’t run. I can’t let you trip and fall, thereby increasing the number of people who’ll need the medicine that’s already short on supply.]

Filóre: [Then, with fast walking!]

As she spoke, she took three large strides towards the person who had called out to them, and from there, as if forgetting about the reason for her fast walking, Filóre broke out into a sprint, causing Heinkel to scratch his head.

Then, clicking his tongue, he hurried to chase after the back of his reckless master.

△▼△▼△▼△

???: [――You’re a harder worker than I thought you’d be, you know?]

At the time of day when orange beams of the setting sun flowed in through the large clerestory, a voice called out from behind Heinkel while he was glaring at some documents in a room of the church.

When he turned around, the one staring at him from the entrance to the room was a man of slender figure and gentle features―― a clergyman of the Church of the Divine Dragon, and the one charged with acting as Filóre’s bodyguard, Tiga Rauleon.

Before her participation in the Royal Selection, it seemed like he had accompanied Filóre as one of her attendants; upon Heinkel’s appointment as her Knight, the two of them met for the first time, and since then have run into each other quite frequently.

As one would expect, Tiga’s initial impression towards Heinkel was the worst―― no, that was not a matter limited to just Tiga, the same could be said for all the people in Filóre’s vicinity. In reality, the only person who welcomed Heinkel’s appointment as her Knight, was Filóre herself.

Heinkel: [Well, that’s only natural. Anybody would react like that, hell, even me.]

Looking at it objectively, Heinkel’s current position was far beyond his measure.

Even at her best, Filóre was already reckless, and caused unceasing worry to those around her, so placing someone like Heinkel, with all the baggage and infamy that came with him, so close to her, was an act that no person with any level of judgment could possibly accept.

Regardless of Filóre’s own “Dragon’s Roar”, it would have likely been more difficult to find anyone who had actually been convinced of this than those who had not.

Tiga: [――? What’s with the sudden distant look? Did you not hear my snide remark?]

Heinkel: [No, I heard it alright, and I sympathize with you all. Even though it’s probably already hard enough being Miss Filóre’s attendant, being forced to take someone like me along too is, well…]

Tiga: [If you can understand that, I would’ve liked you to have politely turned her down to begin with.]

Heinkel: [Can’t argue with that. That would’ve been the proper answer for an adult, but…]

Cutting his words short there, Heinkel hesitated on whether to finish what he was about to say. But, pressed by Tiga’s gaze for the words that followed, he reluctantly opened his mouth.

The reason he had not refused the hand Filóre had offered him, was as plain as day.

Heinkel: [Well, it’s something like an ignoble obsession, a far cry from any mature judgement.]

If adults were people who could accurately discern where to call things off and end them, knowing when to give up, then Heinkel was a horribly wretched creature who had failed to fully grow into an adult.

But, on the other hand, the adult whom Heinkel had admired more than anybody else in this world was a person who never let go of the sword until the very end of the end, cutting through even impossibility itself while never giving up on the things that he loved.

That was something he had yearned for, something he would never be able to reach, something that not even the tips of his fingers would ever be able to touch upon.

That might have been the genesis of Heinkel’s curse. ――Though even if he were to talk about this, Tiga likely would not be interested in the slightest.

Tiga: [――. I’ve done some digging into your situation. Don’t think ill of me. I don’t want anyone dangerous being by Filóre’s side. Besides, part of it’s already quite the well-known tale.]

However, at the tone imbued into Tiga’s following words, Heinkel raised an eyebrow.

He had lived a long time examining people’s expressions, so he knew the delicate nature that existed in the subtleties of negative emotions filling the likes of contempt, ridicule, pity, and sympathy. That was precisely why it made him want to incline his head.

After all, within Tiga’s voice, there had unmistakably been a hint of concern for Heinkel.

Tiga: [That thing you’ve been scowling at with a glum look for a while, is it Filóre’s itinerary? It’s quite difficult to get that girl to stick to her schedule, isn’t it?]

Paying no mind to his suspicions, Tiga stole a glance at the documents from behind, before making an appropriately insightful comment about Filóre.

In fact, tomorrow’s schedule―― with activities such as making courtesy rounds as a Royal Candidate, and fulfilling her duties as a Saintess of the Church, Filóre’s day to day had a dizzying busyness to it. Even with what was not written down on the itinerary, she would attend the divine service that coincided with sunrise in the morning, and after she finished her prayers, she would voluntarily lend an ear to the people who visit the church in search of counsel.

Heinkel: [And in the end, she’s the type who’ll absolutely never overlook any problem that presents itself to her. If she comes across a stray child by the roadside, or an elderly person facing difficulties carrying something, her plans for later will be doomed.]

Tiga: [Ah, I know what you mean. One time in the past, Filóre went missing, and it turned out that she had gone off to help an elderly person carry something, accompanying them three major streets away, before being treated to tea in their home and coming back.]

Heinkel: […As long as her title is Saintess, it should be fine. Though actually, the moment she gained the title Saintess, doing stuff like that was plenty reckless.]

Now that she had become a Royal Candidate, she could no longer do as she had been until that point.

When one gains an irreplaceable role, it comes with tasks that cannot be delegated. Such was expected of Filóre too, and it went without saying which thing had a greater degree of importance.

It went without saying, but――,

Heinkel: [It’s not like Miss Filóre wants to neglect her duties as a member of the Church either, and on top of that, she also wants to devote herself to being a Royal Candidate… it’s all way too excessive.]

Being made to accompany that enthusiasm, Heinkel had to keep busily running about all over the place.

In place of Filóre, who was always poking her head into everything, he was utterly swamped with work that did not befit a first Knight in the slightest, pondering the best person to assign any given problem that emerges to, in order to best get it solved, rescheduling her delayed plans, making apologies to those who were scheduled to meet with her, and preparing in advance the documents and proposals that she would likely need next.

In fact, ever since he had become Filóre’s Knight, the opportunities for him to draw his sword had numbered zero.

Tiga: [Even so, while Filóre attends service every morning, it seems like you never skip out on practice, huh? Though, I’d made the assumption that you surely wouldn’t be a morning person.]

Heinkel: […You think someone who’s bad at waking up early would ever be fit as a Knight?]

Tiga: [I see, it’s seeming more and more like I’d be ill-suited to it. I’m glad the grand duty of being a Knight didn’t end up falling to me. Either way, I probably wouldn’t be able to deny my lack of strength.]

While adjusting the hat on his head, Tiga analyzed himself in a carefree manner, and Heinkel examined him through the corner of his eye.

Heinkel: [Lack of strength, huh.]

To be honest, Heinkel was unable to agree with Tiga’s comment just now.

To begin with, wearing a curved blade by his waist, Tiga was strong enough to be appointed as Filóre’s bodyguard, and even judging by Heinkel’s eyes, his strength was nothing insignificant. His physique was flexible and well-tempered, and the way he carried himself showed that he also had ample real combat experience; above all, he possessed an outstanding grit that would not be perturbed by anything.

He was neither a swordsman nor a Knight, however, he was a warrior. ――That was Heinkel’s appraisal of him.

Be that as it may――,

Heinkel: [So, how are your wounds?]

Tiga: [Hmmm, I guess I can’t say I’ve fully recovered yet. Still, they’ve gotten quite a bit better, but they were quite deep gashes to begin with… As expected, her alias of Valkyrie isn’t just for show.]

Heinkel: [The one who killed Sir McMahon and fled the scene, Duchess Karsten, huh…?]

Tiga gave his answer while patting the side of his torso through his clothes, causing Heinkel to furrow his brow.

The name he had voiced belonged to none other than the very person responsible for inflicting the deep wound upon Tiga’s flank, who was considered to have lit the fuse on the maelstrom of mayhem enveloping the Royal Capital at the moment.

――Crusch Karsten, also known as the Valkyrie, who at first, had been the front runner to win the Royal Selection. And now, she was wanted for being the leading perpetrator behind the assassination of the central figure of the Council of Wise Men, Miklotov McMahon, her whereabouts under pursuit all throughout the Kingdom.

The incident itself had come as quite the shock, but what he found truly incomprehensible was the fact that Natsuki Subaru, who ought to have been Emilia’s Knight, had also been deemed a wanted fugitive for his complicity in Crusch’s actions.

Furthermore, complicity was not the only charge he was facing, as he had even been placed under the exceedingly unbelievable suspicion of being none other than the Sin Archbishop of Sloth.

Accompanying that, both Emilia, who was suspected of harboring rebellious intentions towards the Royal Castle, and Felt, who was unable to dispel the doubts regarding the falsification of her identity, had been taken into custody at the castle, and the members of both Camps fled the Royal Capital―― at that juncture, gargantuan Witchbeasts had been set loose in the town, and the Sword Saint had been mobilized to bring the situation under control.

All of that had already transpired before Heinkel was brought to the Royal Capital, and even now, those events continued to spread a nightmarish chaos throughout not only the Royal Capital, but throughout the entire Kingdom.

Heinkel: [By now, the stark atmosphere of the Royal Capital will be something that goes down in the Kingdom’s history. On the streets, the Knights and the guards all have an imposing air about them, and the townsfolk have nothing cheerful to talk about, so spend all their time just keeping their heads down.]

Tiga: [For the people who have a choice, leaving the Royal Capital is also possible. But, those who don’t are an overwhelming majority. To be honest, the Church is also the busiest it’s been in years.]

Heinkel: [And, that also strengthens the support for Miss Filóre, huh?]

Tiga: [I’m not fond of that way of thinking. Not just me, but Filóre too.]

As Heinkel threw in a cynical remark, Tiga sharpened his gaze upon him.

It seemed like that was not intended as a joke, and it was something that had seriously displeased him, so Heinkel raised both his hands to demonstrate his capitulation.

But, regardless of Tiga’s feelings, in practice, that was how things were progressing.

The more chaos spread in the Kingdom, the more people’s belief in the Royal Castle would be sprained, with their hearts instead beginning to take to the Church that worshipped the Divine Dragon, which had continued to safeguard the Kingdom with a proven track record.

As a result, that had unmistakably become a tailwind for Filóre, who had gotten a late start.

And, for Heinkel too, with his position as Filóre’s Knight, it was certainly something that ought to inspire deep emotion within him, but――,

Heinkel: [Honored Father…]

Across Heinkel’s mind as he muttered, there flashed the existence of Wilhelm, his biological father whose whereabouts were currently unknown.

Crusch was wanted by the authorities for the crime of Miklotov’s assassination, and Wilhelm, who had served her, was one of the relevant parties who had disappeared from the Royal Capital. It was conceivable that he had reconvened with his master, and was assisting her on the run, but it went without saying that they were at an overwhelming disadvantage.

Of course, if it was the famous Sword Demon, he might very well end up cutting through any adversity with that sword of his. Though it was not as though such dream-like expectations did not reside within Heinkel.

Tiga: [You also have it tough, don’t you, Heinkel-san.]

As though he had sensed Heinkel’s inner heart from his mutter and expression, Tiga shrugged.

Having it tough, that comment was probably right. But, if he were to bring that up, the entire Astrea Family had been fragmented ever since Heinkel had joined Priscilla’s camp.

Heinkel: […My own difficulties aren’t anything important. The only problem is that this might cause trouble for Miss Filóre. My honored father and my son… they’re both fully grown men. It’s only natural that everyone wipes their own ass, right?]

Tiga: [――. At the very least, your father was not present at the scene where I crossed blades with Duchess Karsten. It would be good if it turns out the suspicions against your father are unfounded.]

Tiga spoke those words and patted him on the back in encouragement, and after Heinkel hesitated on how to respond, he half-heartedly returned nothing but a crude “Ahh”.

The comment about Wilhelm not having been present there, it was something he could have figured out even if it had not been expressly stated. If Wilhelm had been there, and Tiga had ended up crossing swords with him, Tiga would no longer exist in this world today.

Besides, there was one other reason why his reply had been so vague. And, that was something he would absolutely never reveal to Tiga.

――After all, it was because within Heinkel, a seedling of indelible distrust towards the Church of the Divine Dragon had begun to sprout.

△▼△▼△▼△

――Within the current Kingdom of Lugunica, the role fulfilled by the Church of the Divine Dragon was a major one.

To begin with, the Kingdom of Lugunica was under the protection of the Divine Dragon Volcanica, and with such stability and protection of the nation promised to them, they had continued to thrive until today.

That alone was enough to naturally fill the majority of the Kingdom’s citizens with feelings of reverence towards the Divine Dragon, so inevitably, it also led to their unconditional faith in the Church of the Divine Dragon.

Heinkel was no exception to that, and that was precisely why when his wife fell into a slumber from which she never awoke, he began making frequent visits to the church, placing his belief in the house of prayer and miracle.

Regrettably, Heinkel’s prayers had borne no fruit, and he had gone on to commit a momentous transgression such that he could no longer bring himself to face the Divine Dragon or its followers. Since then, he had grown distant from the Church, hence why he could not help but scoff at how ill-suited his current position was.

But once he finished deploring that foolishness of his, Heinkel had no choice but to confront it directly. The distrust towards the Church of the Divine Dragon burgeoning within himself―― regarding the existence of Filóre. To be precise, regarding the Church’s intentions in having Filóre participate in the Royal Selection.

Appointed as her Knight, what had become painfully clear to him from observing Filóre at such a close proximity, was that she possessed an innate goodness with no ulterior motives whatsoever, to the point it was somewhat frightening.

In absolutely everything, no matter who stood before her, Filóre would always give her all, and ignoring her concerning sense of judgment when it came to naming Heinkel as her Knight, whenever she was pressed for a decision, rather than panicking, she made her choice on her own responsibility, possessing the ability to take action in order to bring those decisions to fruition.

That was why she was always talking, always laughing, always crying, and always on the move. ――The talent of individual virtue capable of mobilizing one’s surroundings just by speaking one’s desires, that was unmistakably the blood pedigree of the Lugunican Royal Family.

Filóre herself did not have an answer as to whether she was truly the royal princess who had gone missing fifteen years prior or not, and she claimed that she did not desire one, but――

Heinkel: [――There’s no way that there are two princesses.]

Since Heinkel had been intimately familiar with Prince Ford Lugunica―― with the father of the missing princess, and the younger brother to the late King Randohal Lugunica, he had no doubts about that.

Ford did not have twins or triplets, his daughter was unmistakably one person.

And, on the precipice of that night fifteen years ago, that singular individual had vanished from the Royal Castle.

The missing royal princess―― it was impossible that she could be anyone other than Felt or Filóre, who had both risen to the stage as Royal Candidates.

Henceforth, someone was plotting. ――Filóre and Felt, in order to prop up either of the two girls as a survivor of the Royal Family, and use them for some ulterior purpose.

When he thought about it like that, and considered the circumstances leading to Filóre’s participation in the Royal Selection, he had no choice but to bear a strong distrust towards the Church of the Divine Dragon.

However――,

Heinkel: […Just what the hell do I even want to do?]

Pondering the matter to this extent, Heinkel’s thoughts came to a standstill as if in fear.

It was as if he was surrounded by a heavy fog with poor visibility as the sunset was drawing ever close, and yet still chose to do absolutely nothing about it; an exceedingly foolish act.

However, within that dense fog, there existed a light that Heinkel had never stopped yearning for over many long years. If he were to take a step in the wrong direction, he might lose that light to eternity.

For that reason, he could not move. He could not bring himself to move. In fear of making a definitive, fatal mistake.

△▼△▼△▼△

――Ultimately, he remained unable to find an answer, with time being the only thing to flow.

After Heinkel and Filóre had entered into a relationship of master and servant, time simply continued to pass, first a few days, which then turned to weeks, and before long a month had passed.

During that time, the Filóre Camp reestablished the flow of resources which had stagnated due to the Royal Capital’s turmoil, responding to the requests raised by the chapels and treatment centers in many locations, steadily increasing support for her as a Royal Candidate. As for Heinkel, his distrust towards the Church had still yet to be dispelled, however, since it was not as if he could do anything that hindered Filóre, he ended up spending day after day constantly running away from his looming apprehensions, merely focusing all of his attention on dealing with the problems before him.

However, while her activities in the Royal Selection were underway, the two matters that Filóre herself hoped to resolve above all else, had not made even the slightest bit of progress.

Heinkel: […Another one came back, huh?]

In one of the rooms of the church, looking down at the mountain of documents piled up atop the desk, and ascertaining the presence of a sealed letter which he had grown so used to seeing, Heinkel frowned in exasperation.

On the opposite side of that desk littered with papers, the woman who was stifling her yawn while working―― Sakura Element, contrary to her seemingly unmotivated attitude, briskly sorted the documents by sender, and arranged them such that the letters could be easily processed and reviewed.

With her sleepy eyes, and her languid demeanor, she glanced at Heinkel,

Sakura: [Yes, it would appear sooo. As per usual, it’s helpful that their replies are so quick, buuut as for the contents… ahhhh, it looks like they deferred us once agaaain.]

Heinkel: [Deferred, huh? How many times is that now?]

Sakura: [Ummm, the letters we’ve sent to the Royal Castle, both long and short, total forty-seven. The ones we’ve sent to the Church total thirty-two, plus, there are also things like additional materials or appended affidavits, and since Filóre-chan is such a proactive correspondent, it would seem that we’ve long since surpassed one hundred leeetters.]

While sorting letters with a single hand, Sakura skillfully checked her record book on the edge of the desk with her other hand. Fed up by her answer, Heinkel heaved a sigh.

With the persistence to surpass a hundred, Filóre had been sending unsolicited letters to the Royal Castle and the Church almost every day―― the contents were, decidedly, requests for meetings with Emilia and Felt, who were both in custody at the castle, and for them to be granted another hearing. Her other request was for permission to use the sacrament in Filóre’s possession to perform treatment on the victims of the Witch Cult remaining in the Watergate City of Pristella.

Filóre was tenaciously fighting on both fronts, attempting to go through all the official procedures necessary, however――,

Heinkel: [Even with all this, why won’t those guys just nod their heads yes? Setting aside the meetings with Emilia-sama and Miss Felt, there ought to be value in trying to help with Pristella. Or maybe, is there some sort of mistake with our paperwork?]

Sakura: [My myyyy, do you suspect I made an oooversight? In that case, I must be a terrible nuisance, making Filóre-chan waste her efforts on one hundred leeetters.]

Heinkel: [I was just pondering aloud. I don’t doubt you. If you were that incompetent, there’s no way you could’ve gotten a title as important as personal secretary to a Saintess.]

Sakura: [Is that sooo? Though, I think it’s also completely possible for it to be something like riding a parent’s coattails, you knowww? Don’t you think so? Deputy Commander of the Royal Guard Heinkel-chan?]

Heinkel: [――. Don’t attach “-chan” to old men, Sakura-chan.]

Sakura: [I’ll defer your request for nowww, Heinkel-chan.]

Giving a reply with no intention to grant his request, Sakura handed the letter that had been sent by the Royal Castle over to Heinkel. Even if he closed his eyes, the contents on its unfolded page were exactly what he had expected would be written there.

At present, the Council of Wise Men were in the midst of carefully deliberating over the requests, so they wished for them to wait for the time being until a conclusion was reached. ――Pertaining to both the treatment of the two being held in custody, and to the use of the sacrament for Pristella, the wording had merely been shifted slightly, and the ultimate answer remained unchanged.

Heinkel: [They won’t reject us. But they won’t approve us either. Just how long do they plan on keeping this up?]

Sakura: [Who’s to sayyy? That’s something for the high and mighty up in the Royal Castle to decide, aaafter all. The situation is what it is, so isn’t everyone just being extra carefuuul?]

Heinkel: [They’ve gone way past the definition of careful at this point. Miss Filóre is also at her limit, and lately she’s been constantly insisting that her heart is being scraped away.]

Sakura: [That sure sounds like how Filóre-chan would phrase iiit.]

Sakura placed her hand over her mouth and giggled, but unfortunately, Heinkel felt no inclination to laugh in agreement with her. Rather, when he saw Filóre’s increasingly forced liveliness day after day, when it was so obviously painful for her, made him feel depressed in turn.

Heinkel: [If the Castle’s no good, how about the Church? Miss Filóre is a Saintess, isn’t she? Can’t she decide for herself who she uses her own Sacrament on?]

Sakura: [She can’t deciiide. It isn’t something so cheap, aaafter all.]

Asserted so definitively, Heinkel was slightly taken aback.

One by one, Sakura tapped her finger on documents split into three piles on top of the desk, and began, “Listeniiing?”

Sakura: [To begin with, “Saintess” isn’t an official rank within the Church, you knowww? It is a special title bestowed upon adherents who have received the Divine Dragon’s favor particularly strongly. Everyone expresses gratitude to them, and they are seated in front of even the high and mighty at ceremonies, buuut, it’s not like they have a seat or any powerful influence at the Holy Synod where the big shots of the Church gather… that’s just how it iiiis.]

Heinkel: [And despite that, they’re treated publicly as the face of the Church.]

Sakura: [Being a symbol that visibly supports the faith of the people is also an important job of a Saintess, aaafter all. That said, even if you were to try to assign Filóre-chan just the duty of acting as an obedient symbol, it would probably be more difficult than teaching the Dragon’s tail to sit stiiiill.]

He could not help but agree to that, but the explanation that preceded the conclusion did not sit right with him.

After all, in the current situation, when Filóre was not responsible for her duties as a Royal Candidate, she was acting a symbol of the Church of the Divine Dragon in the form of a Saintess―― it was a nasty way of putting it, but he could not see it as anything but an implicit expectation that she must carry out her role as mere decoration to the fullest.

Sakura: [Surprisingly, I believe Filóre-chan would be rather suited to being the Monarch, you knowww? That attitude of yours, Heinkel-chan, is also the result of having been enchanted by Filóre-chan’s caliber as a ruler.]

Sakura, who smiled as she looked through his inner heart in his silence, was a poor matchup for Heinkel.

That competence which did not match her appearance and demeanor, could be sensed in all aspects of her conduct. He found Tiga to be the creme of the crop as a bodyguard of the Church, but in Sakura’s case, far from simply being the creme of the crop as a civil officer dispatched by the Church, it seemed as if she was truly among just a handful of exceptionally competent individuals.

In reality, while it was Filóre’s correspondent pen that had written enough letters to reach a count of one hundred, the one to prepare the documents and everything necessary for that, taking all the proper procedures, had been entirely Sakura, and as a relevant party within the Church of the Divine Dragon, she had her hands reached out to nearly all of its divisions.

Heinkel: [As long as they have you, it seems like the Church would generally be able to function well.]

Sakura: [Why, you’re giving me too much creeedit. Unlike Filóre-chan, I’m really unable to put on the kind of face that would give hope to the maaany. Besides, an organization that would entirely falter on the mistake of a single person would be far too dangerous and wouldn’t be able to cooooperate.]

Heinkel: […I see, that’s pretty modest of you.]

Sakura’s answer, given with a wave of her hand, appeared to be a provocation of sorts against the monarchy.

In order to compensate for such an absence, the Kingdom of Lugunica had the Council of Wise Men, but in the current situation, where even the actions of that Council seemed to have dulled, he had no words to give in response, even as a scrap of a Knight of the Kingdom.

Heinkel: [Though, it’s being said that with the death of Sir McMahon, they’ve been in turmoil…]

It was not as though he had witnessed the Council of Wise Men deliberating up close, but Miklotov had certainly been their central figure who always served as the mediator. But, it was not as though the other capable individuals in the council had no influence or say, and starting with Sir Bordeaux Zergev, who would always burst out into overtly heated debates, there ought to have been a flourishing exchange of opinions and viewpoints.

As a matter of fact, the problems concerning the Royal Capital and Royal Castle did not number just one or two, and even in the absence of Miklotov, they remained capable of swiftly dealing with those just as they had before.

In other words, the only matters being kept in a state of uncertainty were the two cases that Filóre was proactively trying to take part in―― as for what that meant, Heinkel too was none the wiser.

Heinkel: [Is the reason why the Church doesn’t approve Miss Filóre’s use of the Sacrament… because it’s involved with the matter of Duchess Karsten being wanted?]

Sakura: [I guess I can’t deny iiit. As a matter of fact, it’s considered a problem that Filóre-chan used the Sacrament without going through the Holy Synod first, so it seems like they’re debating revoking recognition of her as a Saintess, aaafter all.]

Heinkel: [They can revoke her being a Saintess!?]

Sakura: [As per the rules. I don’t think it’s ever been put into practice, thooough. She made it out safe this time, buuut if it’s already been raised for discussion once, she mustn’t get too comfortable, you knowww?]

Sakura spoke without a care, but once again, Heinkel could not help but be shocked.

Filóre’s independent decision, which had sent great tremors through the Royal Castle, seemed to not only be a considerable deal for the Church of the Divine Dragon too, but was also something that placed even Filóre’s own position in jeopardy.

Thus, after having gone so far as to treat Crusch with the Sacrament, for her to then become a wanted fugitive for perpetrating the assassination of Miklotov, the situation was naught but a headwind for Filóre.

Heinkel: [When something you try to do ends up backfiring, I know that feeling all too well…]

Sakura: [Aren’t you getting rather eaaager? Ahhh, but that’s only natural, isn’t iiit? Filóre-chan’s license to use the Sacrament is a matter of life or death for you too, right, Heinkel-chaaaan?]

Heinkel: [――――]

Sakura: [Or perhaps, is it a result of you getting used to being Filóre-chan’s Knight?]

At the gaze and voice that seemed to be mocking him, Heinkel loudly snorted.

Unfortunately for Sakura, Heinkel had no obligation to answer her sadistic sarcasm. Of course, it was the truth that he wished to verify as soon as possible if the power of Filóre’s Sacrament would be capable of saving his wife―― Louanna.

But――,

Heinkel: [When it comes to the people waiting in Pristella, it’s not ambiguous as to whether it’ll be effective or not, rather, it’s a matter of good results being expected. If the lack of permission is the only thing determining whether they’ll be saved or not, it’s only natural to want it to be approved immediately.]

Sakura: [You’re prioritizing others over yourself? Heinkel-chan, were you always such a good person?]

Heinkel: [That’s not what I said. Even though waiting for something can be a salvation, being kept waiting isn’t anything of the sort.]

Sakura: [――I suppose sooo.]

In their tit for tat, Heinkel voiced his true feelings as if spitting them out, however as Sakura responded to him, the tone of ridicule had vanished from her voice.

He found that dubious, but even when examining her expression and eyes, Heinkel was unable to perceive any such changes that had made him feel that way, so it seemed he was merely overthinking things.

Either way――,

Sakura: [――Shouldn’t we just fulfill our duties in siiiilence? If we do that, I’m sure there will be at least one good thing that comes our wayyyy.]

For someone who was a member of the Church of the Divine Dragon, it felt to Heinkel far too modest a murmur, yet at the same time, one that was terribly sincere.

△▼△▼△▼△
