Filóre: [――I’ve decided! If even writing one hundred letters isn’t going to cut it, I’m going to personally deliver the one hundred and first letter! If I make sure to look them in the eye as I make my request, it’ll surely be difficult for them to refuse!]

And, at the words of Filóre, spoken with a face as if she had received some divine revelation from the Dragon, her Knight, bodyguard, and secretary were each forced to accompany her to the Royal Castle.

Working herself up and believing this time would surely be the one, Filóre’s attitude was something to be esteemed, but――,

Filóre: [――I just don’t get it!!]

The moment she stepped out of the reception and into the chalky white corridor, Filóre raised her voice as if to say her patience had reached its limit.

Hearing her indignant voice echo throughout the hall of Royal Castle, the civil officers and employees passing by looked at her in surprise. And cognizant of them all, Tiga placed his index finger to his lips,

Tiga: [Filóre, you’ll stand out too much if you start shouting in a place like this. If your words just now reached the ears of the higher ups, you won’t be turned away at the reception next time, but at the very entrance hall.]

Filóre: [I mean, how can they treat us like this!? Even though we told them we’d prepare everything necessary if they could just tell us what was insufficient, it’s always “this is still under consideration”, “that is on hold”, or “that remains up in the air” for everything…! Just what in the world are we supposed to do!]

Sakura: [I guess there isn’t anything that particularly needs to be added or fiiiixed.]

Filóre: [In that case, they ought to just let us through!]

Heinkel: [――From the beginning, they never had any intention of listening.]

Angrily voicing her complaints, Filóre turned around at Heinkel’s words. Tears were welling up in her ruby eyes, but Heinkel did not have a handkerchief on hand to wipe them.

In place of that handkerchief, he gave her the answer she desired without carefully choosing his words.

Heinkel: [The reason we’re being stopped is neither a deficiency in our documents, nor a failure to meet some conditions. Miss Filóre, the thing they want is for you to give up, and to stop bringing this discussion up to them.]

Filóre: [That sort of thing, that sort of thing is strange! Who would even think something like that?]

Heinkel: [Yeah, that’s what I think is the problem too.]

Filóre appeared as if she was throwing a tantrum, but given that she had already done everything she possibly could have before throwing a tantrum, there was naught else she was allowed to do beyond throwing a tantrum.

As a matter of fact, the question that Filóre currently harbored was something that Heinkel had also been unable to find an answer for, and the inexplicability of it all had only continued to increase over this month and a half.

Heinkel: […You’d think that the stage was being set way too conveniently.]

In all honesty, excluding the fact that Filóre’s entrance was delayed in the Royal Selection, everything else felt like it had been thoroughly set up by the Church of the Divine Dragon.

However, upon opening the lid on that, while it was certainly Filóre’s own actions and virtue that had been steadily increasing support for her within the tumultuous Royal Capital, when it came to the visit to the Watergate City that would definitively solidify her support base―― it was none other than the higher echelon at the Church, the Holy Synod, that would not grant her permission.

If they truly wanted to make Filóre the Monarch, then it was a measure they undoubtedly ought to take.

Despite that, rather than supporting this path, the Church of the Divine Dragon maintained a position that seemed to obstruct it, and the movements of the Council of Wise Men did not side with Filóre either.

Having come to this, the distrust Heinkel harbored toward the Church had begun to intensify in a form that differed to what it had been initially.

Merely, even if his distrust toward the Church intensified in new ways, there were also aspects that remained unchanged. ――It was the fact that Filóre was an immature child who needed an adult to take her side.

Tiga: [Filóre, I understand your feelings, but let’s return for now.]

Urged on by Tiga’s gentle voice, Filóre withdrew in frustration and began walking.

The staff of the Royal Castle who passed them on the way to the entrance all halted their steps upon seeing Filóre, and performed courteous bows.

As a Royal Candidate, and as a Saintess, there was no falsehood in the sentiments of reverence directed her way.

Even so, it was an irony that not a single one of her requests was approved.

Then, carrying forward an oppressive silence as they turned the corner of the corridor――,

Heinkel: [――――]

Grasping the figure of the person walking in their direction, Heinkel reflexively swallowed his breath.

Heinkel: [――Reinhard.]

Before he could even think, the breath he had swallowed spilled out with the sound of that name.

Clad in the white uniform of the Knights, the red haired youth with the Dragon Sword at his waist―― Reinhard van Astrea, trained his gaze straight upon the one who had called out his name.

Naturally, their mutual blue eyes, representative of their blood relation, crossed gazes.

Reinhard: [It has been quite some time, Father.]

Heinkel: […Yeah.]

Even he cursed how pathetic of a reply that had been.

He had been caught completely off guard. Preoccupied with the things on his mind, the unforeseen nature of the encounter rendered him unable to immediately whip out the nasty remarks and verbal abuse he otherwise ought to have had prepared.

Ultimately, unable to settle on any words other than that moronic answer, a silence fell between the father and son.

Reinhard: [――――]

To Reinhard’s rear, he was being accompanied by two individuals clad in the white uniforms of the Guard. At a glance, one might say they were subordinates accompanying the Sword Saint for his duties.

But, rather than on their surroundings, the gazes of the two were unceasingly concentrated on Reinhard’s every action.

Above all, Heinkel had no recognition of the faces of those Knights. ――At the very least, they were Knights of unclear origin, whom Heinkel did not know.

For what reason were these Knights accompanying Reinhard――,

Filóre: [――! Reinhard! Perfect timing! I had wanted to talk to you!]

Trampling straight onto the murky atmosphere between father and son, Filóre rushed over to Reinhard. The Knights behind him poised themselves in response, but Reinhard reined them in by raising a single hand.

Reinhard: [Filóre-sama. Looks like you are paying a visit to the Royal Castle today.]

Filóre: [Yes. I came to talk about Emilia, Felt, and the matter with Pristella. But, more importantly than what I have to say right now, I want to hear from you.]

Reinhard: [From me, is it?]

Filóre: [Yes, that’s right. How’s Felt? You must be meeting her every now and then, right?]

Reinhard: [――――]

As she closed the distance on him without any restraint, Reinhard silently held his breath.

Eventually, Reinhard gave a slow shake of his head, pronouncing “No”.

Filóre: [Umm? That’s… do you mean you’ve yet to see her today?]

Reinhard: [That is not the case. Rather, I have not seen Felt-sama since she was brought into the Royal Castle.]

Filóre: [Since Felt was brought to the castle… not even once!? Even though it’s already been over a month!?]

Filóre’s voice jumped, and both of the Knights to the rear stiffened their shoulders in unison. However, Reinhard simply nodded in silence at Filóre’s response.

But, it was only natural for Filóre to be shocked. This was a completely different dimension compared to Filóre not being given approval to meet Emilia and Felt.

Filóre: [You’re Felt’s Knight, aren’t you? For you to not be able to see Felt, that’s really strange. Don’t you think so?]

Reinhard: [Visitation is forbidden, so it cannot be helped.]

Filóre: [B-but, you want to see her, don’t you? You surely want to speak with her.]

Reinhard: [I am the sword of the Kingdom. Given that I have orders from the Royal Castle, I have a duty to comply with them.]

Filóre: [But you aren’t just the sword of the Kingdom, you’re Felt’s sword too!]

That was――,

Reinhard: [――I am the sword of the Kingdom, Filóre-sama.]

After doing one lap around, the conversation returned to the initial response.

It was not as though Filóre’s words had been insufficient. Neither was it that Reinhard did not understand what she was trying to say.

No matter what he was told, no matter what he felt, Reinhard would never change that answer.

It could not be changed, was perhaps a more accurate way of putting it.

Filóre: [Do you really believe that Felt deceived the Kingdom?]

Reinhard: [No.]

That too had been an instant response, one bereft of any hesitation.

Eyes flickering, before Filóre could ask “So then, why?” in response, Reinhard went on.

Reinhard: [My belief in Felt-sama, and my ability to prove her innocence, are different matters. If I were to renege on my orders, it would only deepen the doubt cast upon Felt-sama, worsening her position even further.]

Filóre: [So, you’re only able to do what you’re told?]

Reinhard: [――――]

At that question, Reinhard chose neither affirmation nor denial.

However, the very fact that he chose neither of the two options, demonstrated precisely where he stood.

Heinkel: [――――]

Heinkel turned his gaze to the two Knights standing behind Reinhard.

It was obvious that they were not Reinhard’s allies. In that case, their job was probably to keep an eye on Reinhard, but what a meaningless precaution.

If Reinhard felt so inclined, the likes of them would be defeated within an instant, then before anyone could even notice, he would vanish from sight and arrive at Felt’s side with nobody in the Royal Castle capable of stopping him.

But, Reinhard would not do that. He could not.

So long as he remained the Sword Saint, that was――.

Filóre: [In that case, at least tell this to Felt.]

In Reinhard’s lapse of silence, Filóre clenched her fist tight, and declared.

Filóre: [I believe in Felt. I believe in Emilia too. Outside of the Royal Castle, there are people who don’t believe the two of them would ever do something like betraying the Kingdom. Please tell her that.]

Reinhard: […Thank you very much.]

Filóre: [It’s fine if it’s a letter too. I’ll even write it myself.]

Reinhard: [However, I cannot promise it. I am also forbidden from delivering words or items to Felt-sama.]

Filóre: [That’s…!]

Reinhard: [Forgive me. I must attend to my next duty.]

Harkening that utterly heartbreaking reply, Filóre’s shapely face twisted out of shape.

However, without folding to Filóre’s reaction, Reinhard left her with a bow, and began moving past them.

Just before his shoulder passed by Heinkel’s, his legs suddenly halted.

Reinhard: [Father, I heard that you have become Filóre-sama’s Knight.]

Heinkel: […Yeah, seems like it. If you got any complaints…]

Reinhard: [――Congratulations.]

Lauded so before he could prattle off any foul language, Heinkel’s words got stuck in his throat.

At a distance where their shoulders were almost touching, Reinhard’s gaze was trained squarely on Heinkel as they faced each other. ――With the face of his son before his eyes, the son who, before he could realize, had caught up to him in height, Heinkel averted his eyes, unable to bear it.

Heinkel: […Whether it’s to be celebrated or not, you couldn’t know.]

Reinhard: [Even so, I am glad that you were chosen, Father.]

Heinkel: [――――]

Hearing those words, Heinkel could not say anything back.

It was not a snide remark, nor irony. From the bottom of his heart, Reinhard was celebrating the fact that someone had chosen his father, who had fallen so low, to be their Knight.

Did he not remember what sort of horrible vilification Heinkel had hurled at him in Pristella?

Had he forgotten that in the same city, Heinkel had turned a blade against his very lady?

Or, perhaps, were even those such trivial matters that they left no scar upon Reinhard’s heart?

Performing a small bow, Reinhard proceeded down the white corridor, the two Knights accompanying him.

Filóre continued to watch over his back in frustration. But Heinkel, unlike Filóre, could not even bring himself to glare at the back of his son, fading into the distance.

△▼△▼△▼△

Tiga: [――Filóre, your remarks towards Reinhard were quite careless.]

Upon returning to the cathedral of the Church of the Divine Dragon, Tiga closed the door to the reception room, and turned back to face Filóre with a stern face.

On the way back from the Royal Castle, silence had reigned over the interior of the dragon carriage, but internally, he must have been contemplating how he ought to scold her.

Tiga: [You might have had the intention of choosing your words carefully, but there were Knights and other servants of the castle back there. If word of it reaches the Council of Wise Men, Filóre, even you will be considered defiant to the Royal Castle.]

Filóre: [It’s best to let them think that. I’m seriously feeling defiant, after all.]

Tiga: [Don’t say those sorta things. I’m telling you that if you also get banned from meetings and visits to the castle, you’ll truly lose your ability to do anything.]

Filóre: [I know.]

Tiga: [If you know, then you shouldn’t be doing such――]

Filóre: [I GET IT!]

Filóre vehemently cut off Tiga’s words.

The menacing air she radiated caused Tiga’s breath to catch, and Sakura also cast her eyes down. Seeing their reactions, Filóre let out a hoarse “I’m sorry”,

Filóre: [I know… I’m sorry. But, it’s because I know that it makes me so excessively angry. If I don’t follow what the people up in the Royal Castle decide, they’ll stop treating me as a Royal Candidate. And if they stop treating me as a Royal Candidate, I won’t be able to save Emilia and Felt. That’s why, I have no choice but to just sit here and wait as I’m told.]

Tiga: [Filóre…]

Filóre: [I’m sorry. I’m well aware that the two of you are only saying all this for my sake.]

Tiga: [――Ahh.]

Filóre: [Let me speak alone with Heinkel-sama for a bit.]

Hearing her request, Tiga returned a hesitant nod.

Sakura exited the room first, and Tiga followed after. The door was shut, thus leaving Filóre and Heinkel as the only two in the room.

Heinkel: [――――]

Atop the desk, a month’s worth of return letters from the Royal Castle were lined up.

Filóre turned her eyes to each and every letter, and eventually, breathed a silent exhale.

Filóre: [Heinkel-sama.]

Heinkel: [What is it?]

Even if it was Filóre, things were likely taking a considerable toll on her.

Her desperate plea remained undelivered, and it could neither be said that her voice had successfully reached Reinhard. Even if she was a girl who proactively attempted any problem that came her way, it was only natural to grow exhausted after such a lack of results.

After his unforeseen encounter with Reinhard, and the word of congratulations he could have never anticipated, Heinkel was also facing extreme mental exhaustion.

Still, with as much mettle as he could muster, he readied himself to try and receive Filóre’s words.

Then, leaning her back against the closed door, Filóre informed Heinkel of a matter she wished to keep hidden from the ears of the departed Tiga and Sakura.

That was――,

Filóre: [――How could we pull off a successful breakout from the castle?]

Hello, it has been quite a while since the last activity report.

The last time was just about 2019, so about 5 years?

Only two seasons of the Re:Zero anime had been unveiled, and in the next activity report it is already “Thank you for Season 3” and “Season 4 is in the works!” It might seem strange to say this, but it is all thanks to everyone’s support.

I mean, based on the stage of the last activity report, I was quite worried I may not have yet started writing Arc 7.

Such an IF route, that diverges from Arc 7, was this time’s Deceiving Life in Another World From Zero .

When it comes to April Fool’s Day updates, I often cannot decide what to write each time until the last minute, but this time I felt it would be a waste not to to tell this story this year, the year the Empire Arc concluded, and so despite all the many chaotic things going on, I somehow managed to finish on time!

Somewhat surprisingly, this was an IF route where the protagonist does not fall into darkness, but as you might guess given his mentality after Arc 6, it would be difficult for him to fall to darkness now, so I think there might not be many more derivational IFs without something exceptional. I can’t say! Since I might end up writing one if I get an idea!

In any case, as is established practice with IF routes, this activity report will cover context that could not be included within the story, so-called superfluous information, thus it will contain spoilers from the get-go, so those who have yet to read the story, please read it first!

※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※

(The following contains spoilers!!)

※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※

■ Natsuki Subaru (Natsumi Schwartz)

・Having not joined the forces of evil this year, he’s a protagonist that appears to have spent his  time comparatively peacefully, did he not? Nonetheless, in the end he was deceived and the bomb was made to detonate, so with the wounds after what was written, confronting and building a relationship with Abel will be rather challenging.

・After Arc 6, he was sent flying to Vollachia from the Pleiades Watchtower due to the clash between the Witch of Envy and Volcanica, and this starting point differs from the main story: the Imperial Capital Lupugana. After suddenly seeming to be trespassing upon the grounds of the castle there, his greatest desire was realized and the awoken Rem did not recognize Subaru. With the stench of the miasma, she was hostile towards him, and with Louis being there too, she had the worst impression; quite a chaotic start. For the time being, realizing he was being pursued, Subaru volunteered himself to act as a decoy so that Rem and Louis could escape, but at this time, a lot of the Empire’s main forces were gathered in the Imperial Capital, so no matter where he went it was only horrific experiences―― and as usual, from that, he seized a glimmer of hope.

・Furthermore, in each IF route, the appearance of the protagonist varies subtly from the main story, but this time, under the pretext of hiding the fact that he is from the Kingdom of Lugunica from those around him, he is almost always crossdressing. After being driven from his throne, a fiancée he has no memory of materializes, and doing whatever she pleases, contributes greatly to Abel’s headache. Due to the scope of his position, Subaru was able to rotate through all sorts of outfits each day.

・As for his relationship with Chisha Gold, whom he never met in the main story, since Abel was able to function as the Emperor with that sort of personality, it goes without saying that his assistant Chisha was abnormally suitable as a supporter, which is proof that he could get along well with Subaru too. In the original route, he was in a position where he had no leeway to do so, and he was continuously in the middle of a quite tense balancing act, but in this case, he got along well with the main Imperial faction from the start, including the Nine Divine Generals, showing he has grown quite a bit as a person, having come to terms with his life in another world.

・Despite her status as a hostage, he had better mental composure at being able to leave Rem in a safe place, and as a result of the frequency of Rem’s doubts of “Why are you going so far?” being much less frequent, the “You’re not a hero” incident did not occur, and the friction with Rem, who lacked her Memories, was somewhat lessened and compromises could be made. Still, he would drive Louis away.

・As always, he exhibited his crossdressing power, made Kafma think, “Just who exactly is this Lady Natumi Schwartz who appeared as a replacement for Natsuki Subaru-dono?”, caused Cecilus to call him Ma’am instead of Boss, and whilst enjoying his life in the Empire thought maybe it would be fine to bring Chisha, who had angered the Emperor so, to Lugunica. However, in the end, he was deceived by his accomplice Chisha, who accomplished his goal. He selfishly decided to take on half the weight of the baton Chisha had entrusted to Abel, and it converged back to the main story of Arc 8―― and at that point, the curtains lowered upon our story.

・From this route, without having built a relationship with Abel, having yet to meet up with the Emilia Camp, and the absences of all sorts of named characters, makes it very likely this Arc 8 would be far more harsh, but naturally I will not be depicting such an IF next year.

■ Rem & Louis (Spica)

・The moment she woke up, a stinking man she did not know proclaimed “I’m your hero”, then in that period of chaos, she was chased by an absurdly terrifying pursuer, put in house arrest as a hostage, and the stinking man who came by often was treated with astounding respect, truly, she was a heroine blown around by fate like fallen leaves at the mercy of the wind.

・At the start, Subaru’s favorability was just as low as in the original story, but since Berstetz had properly informed her about Subaru sacrificing himself in order to save Rem, she was aware that she had become a burden for Subaru, and as a result, the truth was that compared to the original story, the improvement in his initial favorability was faster. Since she was forced to mostly spend her time at the mansion in the Imperial Capital, Subaru did not seem to be casually jumping into life-or-death situations and coming close to death, which was better conditions for Rem, who hates self-sacrifice. However, because they were not given the time to cultivate a bond, Louis and Subaru’s relationship was in a poor shape, and due to that, she harbored endless displeasure towards that attitude of Subaru’s towards Louis.

・In the time she spent at the mansion, she recalled how to use healing magic, and contributed to the recovery of Kafma, who was sidelined due to his injuries. Feeling indebted to her, the militaristic man thanked her with a “Long live Miss Rem!”, and she successfully earned the endorsement and tremendous support of the man practically guaranteed to become the next General First-Class.

・Furthermore, in her life at the mansion, she succeeded in forming a bond with Madelyn, the sullen dragon-girl. In the original story, she snuck her way into Priscilla’s heart, and perfectly exhibiting her innate suitability as a supporter, she managed to acquire a bone flute from that dragon that would entrust her with a flying dragon. It is likely that in this route’s Arc 8, she would raise her voice for the sake of Madelyn, who suffers due to the existence of her loved one, and would help coax out her true feelings and allow her to move forward.

・In addition, she would also meet and become friends with Katya, living in the Imperial Capital, in this route as well.

・On the other hand, regarding Louis, she is still very attached to Rem in this route, and her reaction to Subaru when he comes to see them is similar, however, compared to the original story, he was colder to her, and there was no further progress. Even embarking into Arc 8, it seems unlikely that the name change event will occur.

・While some bonds were forged through the cruelty of the original route, other sentiments could have been cultivated in a more gentle manner. Thus, debating which route would be better for them seems to be nothing but tactless.

■ Berstetz & Ubilk & Kafma

・The main members of the Empire outside of the Nine Divine Generals.

・Berstetz’s objective is rooted in his distrust of Vincent, who was damaging the ways of the Vollachian Empire by not properly producing any heirs. Yet, in this route, Rem was recognized as Subaru’s partner, so there were no attempts at setting up a forced marriage. On the other hand, the reason he kept Madelyn close at hand was because she was an easily managed pawn, and at the same time, also a very likely candidate for Vincent’s partner, so in that sense, that old man is truly a Sword Wolf of Vollachia. Surprisingly, Louis really took to him, and he may have felt such a feeling was not too bad.

・Ubilk acts as counsel in crucial moments as a Stargazer, but thanks to his accomplishments as a Stargazer in the past, when Subaru was treated as a Stargazer of Lugunica, everyone had a rather agreeable mood, like “Ahh, sure sure.” Therefore, Subaru did not seem to realize it, but he might be his hidden benefactor. Since Subaru acted as a substitute where he had originally come along, it seems like he was living a life of leisure.

・Kafma, the epitome of a serious Imperial soldier, could not solve the equation of Subaru=Schwartz, and seemingly perceived Subaru and Natsumi as different individuals. At Chaosflame, he sustained life-threatening injuries and though he withdrew from the front lines, he was able to return due to Rem’s healing magic. He considered himself to be greatly indebted to her and supported her fervently. If anything unpleasant were to happen to her in her job as a healer, he would directly confront the source of it, persistently saying, “I would like you to explain what fault lies with my savior.”

■ Nine Divine Generals

・Since the initial faction Subaru belonged to changed, naturally the following attitudes of everyone changed drastically as well. At the time of Arc 7 of the original story, the Nine Divine Generals were mostly enemies, but in this route many of them were allies from the early stages, which made it a rather easy route. Because he did not oppose Old Man Olbart, Subaru’s number of deaths were likely an order of magnitude lower. Damn terrifyin’, that old man.

・As a result of being deployed to Guaral just like in the main story, Arakiya, who made contact in the earliest stages of the story, became a casualty (a traitor!), and unlike in the main story, there was no event where she was freed from captivity, thus after twists and turns she switched sides.

・It was predetermined that Olbart would lose an arm in Chaosflame and Groovy was absent due to being deployed to the west of the Empire as part of Chisha’s schemes like in the main story. Goz was imprisoned, but in this regard, it was somewhat better than the main story due to Subaru being able to take into consideration his circumstances. Subaru, in his villainess persona, might have occasionally made an appearance and thrown him something to improve his nutrition. There are suspicions that Moguro got along well with Miss Natsumi, given how she casually called him “Mogurocchi”, but what are everyone’s impressions?

・And yet, since they were unable to win over Yorna-san of Chaosflame in this route, the Demon City maintained a policy of independence, aligning with neither the Emperor’s side nor the rebel’s side. Thus, even after arriving at Arc 8, Iris and the King of Thorns would not reunite, and in this aspect, it is evident that it ends in tragedy compared to the main story.

・As discussed in Rem’s section, the bond between Madelyn and Rem had clearly grown, and thus despite suffering from Balleroy’s existence after the Great Disaster, in the end she would listen to Rem’s words and manage to achieve a proper farewell. In that case, Rem might have realized a position like Friend of Mezoreia, which might have been satisfying in its own way.

・Altogether, even though the positions and roles of the Nine Divine Generals change, they seem to be strong individuals whose ultimate survival rates and conditions remain unchanged. However, if the story rushes forth into Arc 8 as it currently stands, all the conditions that relate to the survival of those like Goz, Olbart, Groovy, or Moguro no longer exist, thus there might be a high probability that around half of them are replaced.

■ Cecilus Segmunt

・Despite the starting point having changed from the main story, due to already having been infantilized by Chisha by that starting point, our Ceci was banished to the Gladiator Island to get him out of the way. The truth regarding Cecilus becoming small is that Chisha’s method of shrinking Cecilus was wearing the Mask of the Vicious.

・Picking up Subaru, who washed up upon the Gladiator Island, and having his heart tremble with the premonition that a story was beginning―― unlike the main story, which flowed in such a manner, it starts with Natsumi and Chisha coming to take him away, and with his usual story-focused brain, he perplexes them with theories of narrative like “It wouldn’t be very refined to suddenly join them, so I should refuse them a few times!” That being said, for the person in question, aside from such theories of narrative, he also had his intuitive sense of aesthetics, and that ultimately helped him build relationships with Subaru and Chisha, and thus as one might expect, there is beauty in everything a leading actor does. In addition, in the main story, he called Subaru “Boss”, but due to Subaru never removing his disguise as a woman in front of Cecilus in this route, he was called “Ma’am”.

・The scene where they fight together with Chisha’s trump card of Mask of the Lightning was something I could not find the timing to do in the main story, so I was especially moved to be able to do so here. For the young Cecilus, being able to see his future, perfected self was a huge prize, but since Chisha’s Noh is limited to only reproducing about eighty percent of the original abilities, the boastings of Cecilus, who held impressions like, “I’m gonna be much better in the future!” were actually correct.

・For Chisha, who had intended to announce their parting face-to-face already once before, this route in which he had a reunion and second parting must have been pretty awkward. However, for Chisha, who was probably feeling anxious about whether he could see it through to the end, having that final word was also salvation. Being able to put that second parting into words there could probably be said to be the influence of Subaru, and thus the second parting of those two in this story was truly “Perfect!”

・Incidentally, during the decisive battle for the Imperial Capital, Arakiya was entrusted to him as his opponent, and it seems he successfully engaged in a battle that destroyed not one, but two of the points of the star, as the fiercest battleground of the decisive battle.

■ The People of Shudraq

・Utakata was left behind and wiped out.

■ O’Connell Siblings

・Flop died in the conquest of the Fortress City of Guaral, where poison was used.

・Due to the same poison, Medium wandered between life and death, but with to the effect of her Divine Protection of Morale, she encouraged herself that she could not die until she had gotten revenge for her brother, and lived. However, she was tricked into thinking that the ones who had used the poison were the Imperial Army, and joined the rebels, weeping as she participated in the vanguard hunting down Imperial soldiers.

■ Zikr Osman

・He was killed in the battle for the Fortress City of Guaral and his head was displayed as that of a defeated General.

■ Tanza

・Just as in the main story, the plan she devised to protect Yorna backfired, and her loyalty was viewed as dangerous by a certain werewolf, who disposed of her. As a result, Yorna, who led Chaosflame, fell into a state where she was independent of both Abel and Chisha, and that girl’s desire for Yorna to not participate in the war was realized, at the cost of her life.

■ Pleiades Battalion

・Was not formed.

・As a consequence of Subaru not participating in the Sparka, Hiain, Weitz, and Idra did not come to understand each other and fell to the Guiltylaw’s claws, and were annihilated.

・Since Natsumi and Chisha’s purpose in visiting the Gladiator Island was to retrieve Cecilus, the other gladiators remained there, and Gustav, as the governor, protected His Excellency the Emperor’s life and their Sparka continued.

■ Bandana Bastard and Twin Sword Wielder

・It need not be said that these were Todd Fang and Jamal Aurélie.

・In this route, instead of Abel running into Subaru, he lured the two of them, camping near the forest of the Shudraq, into becoming his allies.

・The Lifeblood Ritual is a matter of whether one can clear the greatest tribulation facing the Shudraq at the time, and with the absence of Subaru, the Witchbeast Elgina did not appear, so the Lifeblood Ritual bestowed upon Abel became repelling the camp where Todd and the others were.

・The two of them were captured during the battle there, and as soon as Jamal figured out Abel’s identity, he immediately surrendered, and Todd, who intended to bide his time and wait for an opportunity to escape, promised to help upon the condition that Abel would repeal the decree to exterminate the wolfpeople and molepeople to the last, after Abel figured out his nature as a werewolf―― all the while completely intending to snatch Katya and escape somewhere.

・With Abel desiring to return to the throne by the shortest path possible, since he had good compatibility in the worst sense with Todd’s rationalism that ignores all emotion, the results included the use of poison in taking Guaral, murdering Tanza in Chaosflame, and afterwards the utilization of guerilla warfare and continuing to inflict disgusting violence. Furthermore, after they captured Arakiya when she was deployed to Guaral, he recommended making good use of her, and took her in, and just like in the main story, they formed a one-sided relationship that Arakiya found not entirely uncomfortable.

・Ultimately, it seems that the future of Jamal becoming Abel’s bodyguard did not change, and it is very likely Todd managed to escape with Katya in the turmoil of the decisive battle at the Imperial Capital, and probably would not appear in Arc 8.

■ Vincent Vollachia (Abel)

・Unlike the original story, he resolutely survived the Lifeblood Ritual, the Fortress City of Guaral, and the Demon City of Chaosflame without the help of Natsuki Subaru, as the unyielding and unassailable Wise Emperor we all know.

・Since he was forced to take more cold-blooded measures than in the main story with Subaru not present, the road back to the throne was drenched in much blood, and the increase in his own psychological burden was immense. And yet, for the citizens of the Empire, this was exactly the way of the Empire, and so they cheered and applauded him like roaring thunder. The Empire is truly terrible.

・Despite numerous sacrifices, such as the Shudrak for starters, Chisha attained his long-cherished desire upon the throne he had finally managed to reach, dealing a serious blow. Furthermore, a fianc é e he did not know showed up saying things like “Stand up for Chisha’s sake!”, to which “What the hell would you know about Chisha!” would lead to an expected development where spittle flies between them.

・After temporarily withdrawing from the capital, a relationship of cooperation should be forged with Subaru just like in the main story. However, since there is nothing other than Chisha binding them together, their relationship is like that of friends of a friend with their treasured mutual friend no longer there. While it seems like they could forge a decently respectable bond, on the other hand, it seems like it would take quite a while for their relationship to become as solid as it was in the main story, and with the muddled state of Arc 8, it seems like it would be quite difficult.

・In my own selfish imagination, after the war, even though he would accept Medium, who contributed greatly to his cause as a demon of vengeance, as one of his consorts like in the main story, she would come to know of the truth about Guaral somehow, and I very much fear she may stab him in an incident like that of Delita and Ovelia. The king does not understand the human heart… [1]

■ Emilia Camp & Priscilla Camp

・Just as in the main story, Emilia, Priscilla and the others managed to enter Vollachia, and were roughly following the same developments. However, due to Subaru’s absence, Al did not accompany the Chaosflame team, and greatly contributed to responding to Madelyn’s attack on Guaral and reducing the damage, primarily around Priscilla.

・Additionally, in this route, Abel’s principles and Emilia’s principles definitely did not mesh well, and thus, with the Emilia Camp not joining Abel and the others, they did not participate in the decisive battle at the Imperial Capital. With the name of “Natsumi Schwartz” reaching the ears of Emilia and the others, Ram, Roswaal, and Otto, who properly understood it as message from Subaru, proposed during their meeting that they should try to get in contact with Subaru, who was apparently there, in the chaos of the decisive battle at the Imperial Capital. To that end, I believe Emilia and the others would finally join the decisive battle at the Imperial Capital, in a similar way to the participation of the Pleiades Battalion in the original story. Incidentally, in this Arc 8, it seems like Subaru would be able to actually witness the reunion between the sisters of Rem and Ram, and I imagine tears would flow like the Great Waterfall.

・In addition, as for the conclusion she would face at the end of Arc 8, it appears it would mirror the same essence and shape of the Azamuku route, that actions with strong conviction and motivation will not be permitted to be altered, even by a power that overthrows fate.

■ Chisha Gold

・Having possessed a golden soul, he was a great liar who deceived even fate. He was the Azamuku route’s protagonist, as well as the scenario’s heroine.

・I must confess, as the author, that I began to write the story this time with the intent of Chisha surviving and Abel dying. However, no matter how hard I tried, Chisha would not let me deviate from his plans. I would not go so far as to say he deceived even me, the author, but he is a character that I have no choice but to admit forced even the author himself to collaborate in his deception, creating this story.

・Since I’ve said pretty much all I want to say on his thoughts and actions in the main story and this IF, I do not have much more to add here. If I had to say something, it would be that the words Chisha could not say on the eve of the decisive battle were the message for Abel that Chisha entrusted to Flop in the main story. However, if he had imparted it to Subaru in that place, he was in danger of leaking his schemes to Subaru, and since he had already decided to have Subaru escape to the Kingdom before the decisive battle at the Imperial Capital at that point, there was no point in telling him that. Additionally, the bond between him and Subaru was, in the beginning, based upon the expectation that he could use his ability as a Stargazer and that he would become an essential asset for Abel in repelling the Great Disaster. However, by the eve of the decisive battle, it had changed significantly. For Chisha, who had decided to have but one master and one friend, this bond did not fit either, but he thought it to be in a unique position that was something close to those.

・As briefly mentioned in Cecilus’s sections, Noh is a copying ability able to reproduce around eighty percent of the abilities of another who has been traced as a “mask”. It is a broken ability that exhibits its true strength in much the same way as shown in the IF route. Despite saying things such as “I lack much fighting strength myself,” when he shows his trump card, he will mercilessly turn into Cecilus. In addition, in spite of it being a trump card, Cecilus will allow him to touch his face if he asks, so it is pretty much a trump card that he can use endlessly. In fact, there is a possibility that some of Cecilus’s valorous acts were actually the deeds of Chisha secretly in the form of Cecilus, but if Cecilus were to be asked about them, he would comment “Did I do that? I feel like I did! I did do that!” and thus no one finds it strange. To begin with, Cecilus’s heroic achievements are pretty buggy, so this addition is really only a rounding error.

・In any case, as a writer who loves visual novels, I am completely satisfied in being able to write something like a simple alternative route, very different from other IF routes thus far. As the author, I also enjoy thinking about what kinds of relationships might be built with Subaru, so I am also very pleased with that.

・In the end, both in the main story and in the IF, Chisha Gold, seeing through to the end what he had decided to do, was undoubtedly a man worthy of the title of Sword Wolf of the Empire――.

And that is about it for what I wanted to say about the Azamuku route!

There are many differences between the main story and Azamuku, but due to the reduced number of named characters, it is to be expected that the damage would be greater. I do not believe either one to be particularly easy though!

Well then, thank you for this year’s April Fool’s Day!

Please continue supporting Re:Zero! See you soon!

--- Azamuku IF – Re: Deceiving Life in Another World From Zero ---

△▼△▼△▼△

Art Sources:

This translation is dedicated to Erifuru , a translator and friend who will be deeply missed.

This is a just barely in-time update for the annual April Fool’s Day project!

The story this time is part of the IF Story series that have been released up till now, but it is a slightly different type of story. Of course, I wanted to write it, so I wrote it as I liked.

What kind of story could it be? I hope you enjoy it and I look forward to seeing you in the afterword!

――It was probably an instance where a single misstep sent the entire journey astray.

With but a single misalignment of gears, the tale twisted askew, and the rails of fate changed course with ease.

When the expected flow of events shifted, the torrent of destiny tossed people around like leaves from a tree.

And yet, what if they still finally found their way unto that changeless shore on the other side, unyielding?

Surely, it was only when a strong, unwavering desire utterly deceived that Commandment.

It was precisely within that once-in-a-lifetime lie that the meaning of that man’s life dwelled.

△▼△▼△▼△

???: [Haa, haa… hk!]

The girl panted as she fled, desperately clutching the child’s hand.

Despite running with all her might, the girl’s speed was lacking. For, within this unfamiliar land, one of her legs was impaired. ――Nay, if one called it an unfamiliar land, then for this girl, the whole world was strange.

This was a place she did not recognize whatsoever, these circumstances were beyond her comprehension, and as for her current situation, she could fathom naught.

Thus――,

???: [Uu! Uu, aau!]

Dragged by the girl’s hand, the child, whose name she did not even know, had been continuously wailing inarticulate cries.

Girl: [――Hk.]

Tightly biting her lips, the girl banished the weakness within her mind and faced ahead.

Indeed, at this moment, everything was unknown to her.. However, certain truths were clear. She knew that she must not let go of this child’s hand, and that she must continue to run forward.

In the midst of this world awash with unknowns, the girl’s instinct cried out for her to flee. Escape was the sole means by which the girl could express her will to resist; a protest permitted to her present self.

Girl: [That, person… hk.]

Whilst experiencing a pain that seared her breath-starved lungs, the girl’s bewildered mind envisioned a single figure. It had the appearance of a boy with black hair and mean-looking eyes, and its very presence evoked both negative impulses as well as strange feelings――,

???: [―― Oh, it’s really an Oni. That’s unusual. ]

Girl: [――Hk.]

That carefree voice suddenly intruded on the girl’s thoughts, sending a tremor throughout her body, and she sharply whirled about.

Mirrored in the girl’s pale blue eyes was a one-eyed woman wearing an eyepatch who was running―― nay, flying beside her. She was a beautiful woman with the animal ears of a dogperson and much of her brown skin exposed to the wind. At the entrance of the woman cutting through the air with a long branch in her grasp, the child that was being dragged behind the girl let out a shriek.

The moment she heard that scream, the girl reflexively attempted to fend off the woman with her free hand.

However――,

Woman: [――? That didn’t connect. It’s a shame, but…]

Off-balance, her swung arm was seized effortlessly, and in turn, she found herself pulled in.

Their faces had drawn so near to one another that the tips of their noses were about to touch, and in the woman’s red eye uncovered by an eyepatch, the girl beheld her own visage in its reflection.

It was an unfamiliar face. ――That was the face of a girl who did not understand the world, let alone herself.

Woman: [I was told to capture you.]

Girl: [――Ah.]

The instant the girl beheld her reflection, the woman lightly tapped the center of her chest with a finger, and the girl felt a minute shock course throughout her entire body.

The action had effortlessly stolen the strength from the girl’s limbs, forcing her to collapse to her knees.

Girl: [Ugh!]

Woman: [That child, too.]

Beside the collapsed girl, the brave child leapt at the woman.

However, the woman caught the strike with the ease of twisting a baby’s hand, and then, that same shock the girl had endured was delivered to the child’s brow, and with an “Aauu?”, she flopped and toppled over as if all her strength had been sapped away.

As a result, the chase sequence starring the girl and the small child reached its anticlimactic conclusion.

Girl: [You, are…]

Woman: [Don’t worry, no harm will… well, I’m not sure. Sorry.]

As the girl crawled toward the dazed child, straining her voice, the woman offered words of apology. But, that was by no means a consolation, as there was no sense of being saved by that apology.

Whether she ought to deem it sincerity or clumsiness, the girl could choose neither.

Slowly but surely, as the child before her slipped into unconsciousness, so too did her own reality begin to fade away.

Woman: [Let’s go, Oni girl.]

Girl: [I, am…]

The sensation of being picked up by the woman was an action she could not resist. As her consciousness gradually faded to white, the girl’s lips trembled feebly.

Being called an Oni failed to resonate with her. That being said, there was another way she had been called――,

Rem: [――Rem.]

That name had been spoken by the black-haired boy enveloped in that dreadful, abhorrent stench.

Perhaps, it was some kind of illusion. ――That above all else, that name somehow felt familiar to her empty self that lacked anything.

△▼△▼△▼△

――Things had taken a troublesome turn.

A combination of dread and vigilance coursed like lightning through Natsuki Subaru’s mind, compelling him to act urgently.

Why, why, why ; he had not even a moment to spare in order to ponder such a question.

He organized his thoughts concerning recent events: the arrival of the opportunity for a long-awaited reunion, and the bitter sorrow that came thereafter when reality had failed to meet his hopes. Suppressing that grief, focusing his mind on the precious people he had been separated from, he steeled his resolve to escape this irrational, senseless impasse―― at least, that was what he ought to do.

And yet――,

???: [Kakakakka! Ya young’uns really are terrifyin’! Even I’ve never seen one with this much recklessness, impossibility, and sheer madness. Amazin’, amazin’.]

The hoarse voice rang out in a hearty laugh, accompanied by a knifehand thrust like steel that struck his heart.

His back was pierced by the knifehand, and as he beheld his own heart torn from his chest, in a tempest of agony and shock, Subaru died instantly.

×  ×  ×

???: [How did a friggin’ human like yourself slip past the watch of us dragons? I don’t know how the frig ’ you did, and that fact I don’t is the height of friggin’ disrespect!]

Bearing a sweet outward appearance, the tantrum of this destructive being was clad in a tempest with a single swing of her arm.

That slender arm did not even need to make contact with him, stirring up a gale which seized the boy’s body and hurled him against the castle walls. Tasting the pain of all of his bones shattering, Subaru died instantly.

×  ×  ×

???: [Deceived… my eyes. Do not understand… how? Scary.]

The shapeshifting statue in the beautiful garden voiced its dread, swinging down an arm that resembled a marble pillar.

Once, then twice, he had managed to evade the arm, but he could not do so forever. The third blow grazed his leg, robbing his body of all mobility, followed by the fourth strike landing a direct blow on him, and as he was compressed to a tenth of his original size, Subaru died instantly.

×  ×  ×

???: [――! Who are you! Don’t you realize whose castle this is, you fool!]

With a gallant, inflexible, righteous fury, sharp thorns flashed like blades.

His whole body was ensnared by purple vines covered in thorns, and as every bit of his flesh was rent asunder, as Subaru’s consciousness was shattered by the unbearable pain of his spilt blood and how the thorns on the vines writhing like they had a will of their own were gnawing at his wounds, he breathed his last.

×  ×  ×

???: [There he is! Don’t let him get away!!]

???: [You villain!]

???: [Do you think you can get away with this!?]

He was cornered by bearers of steel who had flushed out their prey, holding a will to fight that had been honed.

Surrounded on all sides, with neither a place to escape, nor anyone who would lend an ear to his excuses, the thrusting blades pierced his entire body, and suffering all of those mortal wounds, Subaru collapsed and breathed his last.

×  ×  ×

Subaru: [In the first place――]

Subaru gritted his teeth, wondering if he had erred in his choices from the outset, having repeated Death five times.

Subaru had already been alone at the new starting point of Return by Death. ――It may have been a mistake to end up here alone in the first place.

When he thought about how she might be suffering the same things he had even at this very moment, that alone was enough turmoil to crack and shatter his heart.

What was it that he needed?

What possibilities must he secure?

Where was the checkpoint that he must reach?

Walking a tightrope that was far too narrow and unreliable, having to reach the other side no matter the cost, what exactly was it that Subaru must be able to fulfill?

Subaru: [――――]

It was a situation where he must attract attention, yet if Subaru moved carelessly, he would be obstructed by a tough opponent that was far and away beyond his own abilities, and they would take his life all too quickly.

There were a great many enemies. And not a single one had a shred of mercy. ――Subaru’s path was blocked by individuals who had absolutely no qualms about killing their opponents.

In order to break through that, to surmount it, that tiny, minute gap in the possibilities, he would――

Subaru: [――――]

Running over carefully tidied lawns, Subaru headed in a different direction than all the other routes which had been closed off to him, and found an opulent detached palace.

Gaudy and beautiful, yet less gaudy compared the castle that Subaru had just been trying and failing to escape, and he would hope that it had a bit less stringent security.

Accordingly, he should be able to obtain at least a single piece of information. ――With such an intention, Subaru smashed a window in a place void of any signs of people, unlocked it, and tumbled into the Imperial Residence.

In the next instant――,

???: [――You fool.]

He had climbed over the window frame and just put the tips of his toes on the floor.

As soon as he heard that weighty, stern voice, Subaru’s legs were clipped from the side, and he was mercilessly slammed headfirst into the floor.

Subaru: [Oguahh!]

The instant he let out a shriek of pain and his vision flickered red, the worst scenarios flashed through his mind.

After all, up to now, Subaru had repeatedly ended up having his life stolen away from him by completely different people in different ways, all in the span of around ten minutes.

That’s why it was no wonder that, in the midst of the pain, he had resigned himself to it being the same again.

However――,

???: [You, how did you manage to evade the security and get in here?]

The expected arrival of the shock of Death did not befall him, but instead, a question was asked of him.

While grimacing in pain, Subaru lay sprawled out spread-eagle on the floor, and he caught a glimpse of the person who had raised that query to him―― the one who had intercepted Subaru sneaking into the Imperial Residence.

Subaru: [――――]

Standing there, with black hair and black eyes, was a handsome man with tidy features that gave off the impression of a frightening intellect. That individual wearing a crimson outfit that conveyed the quality of its tailoring with a single glance was warily looking down upon Subaru with a gaze as sharp as that of a bird of prey.

That glare usurped his conscious thought, and Subaru froze like he had been pinned down. ――And yet, it was not simply the gaze of the handsome man that had immobilized Subaru.

Handsome Man: [Did you not hear my question? It would be irreverent to not provide any answer.]

With an austere voice and words, the handsome man was about to callously decide Subaru’s fate.

However, rather than this cruel reality, Subaru’s awareness was seized by the strange phenomenon before his eyes―― the profound mystery within the full-length mirror placed beside the handsome man looking down on him.

Upon the mirror, the reflected image of the dark-haired handsome man was different. ――Reflected there was a man, taller than the handsome man with black hair, possessing white hair, white clothes, and a pale face.

As Subaru gasped at the peculiarity of that, the handsome man in reality shut one eye and tapped his foot.

And then, as if an ultimatum, he asked a question once more.

Handsome Man: [There shall not be a third time. Take care, and answer my question.]

Subaru blinked at the overlapping images, and then his consciousness returned to reality.

Then, the figure of the man in white who had just been visible within the mirror a moment prior was nowhere to be seen, and all that remained was the form of the handsome man who stared at him with a dreadfully overbearing attitude.

Seeing this, Subaru swallowed his breath, and then spoke.

Subaru: [――My name is Natsuki Subaru.]

It was an inadequate answer to any of the questions that the handsome man had asked.

Thinking back on it later, even Subaru himself could not think of a proper reason why he had given his name here, had introduced himself without falsifying his identity.

He could only assume that it was an intuitive answer, drawn from his brain which had become confused due to erratically and reflexively accumulating absurd and irrational Deaths over and over again within a short span of time.

Hearing that answer of Subaru’s that could easily strike a nerve with someone, the handsome man――,

Handsome Man: [――Lugunica’s… Lolimancer, is it?]

Yes, he raised his finely shaped eyebrows, and with a hint of bewilderment that did not suit his face, which was like the embodiment of an arrogance that placed all the events of the world within his own palms, he muttered so.

――This itself, was the first misstep.

Natsuki Subaru, who had unexpectedly been sent to the Sacred Vollachian Empire, and “Vincent Vollachia”, the pinnacle of the Land of the Sword Wolves―― it was the meeting of the two whose destinies should never have crossed paths in the first place, comrades who would deceive fate.

△▼△▼△▼△

???: [――I’ve brought them.]

Saying that, the one who brazenly stepped into the office of the Imperial Residence was a young girl with a strangely revealing outfit that showed off her brown skin, dog ears, and an eyepatch over her left eye; she was overloaded with character traits.

Subaru was taken aback by her appearance, but when he saw that she was carrying Rem upon her slender shoulders and an extra person under her arm, he exclaimed “Rem!” as he hurriedly rushed over.

Subaru: [Are you hurt anywhere?… Opossum !]

Eyepatch Girl: [Don’t do that so suddenly, it surprised me.]

As he tried to ensure she was safe, toes drilled into his defenseless solar plexus and he fell in agony.

The girl with the eyepatch had only casually lifted her bare foot, but it was not a matter of the strength of her legs, but rather of the skill to precisely gouge his vitals―― no, it was a brutal, instinctual kick without any such calculation behind it.

However, despite having his organs bored through by the shock, Subaru staggered over to Rem, slung over the girl’s shoulder, and after confirming her breathing and the tinge of red on her cheeks, he heaved a sigh of relief.

Subaru: […It seems like nothing bad. She’ll actually wake up, right?]

Eyepatch Girl: [I only put her to sleep. She’ll wake up soon. This one too.]

Subaru: [I don’t care about that one. If anything, I’d rather she’d stay asleep forever.]

Eyepatch Girl: […Your relationships are… complicated?]

Subaru: [Not at all. Rem is important, that one isn’t. That’s all.]

Subaru glared at the blonde girl being held under the girl’s arm opposite to Rem.

At his declaration, the girl’s one red eye widened and her lips twitched. It seemed like Subaru’s answer was not to her liking in some way, but unfortunately it was his true thoughts.

But it was impossible to mend things between them. ――Unlike the courageous, gentle, hard-working, and compassionate Rem, that girl was a monster who had piled up a mountain of unpardonable sins.

Subaru: [――Louis Arneb.]

With a whisper, Subaru muttered the girl’s―― the Sin Archbishop of Gluttony’s name.

Right now, she seemed to be sleeping, but she was one of the enemies who had thoroughly tormented him during the battles at the Pleiades Watchtower and made him experience hell. It was a mystery as to why she, who was supposed to be an incorporeal entity, had manifested with a body in reality, but there was no way she was up to anything good.

In any case――,

Subaru: [Thank you for not hurting Rem. You are…?]

Eyepatch Girl: [Arakiya.]

Subaru: [Thanks, Arakiya-chan! I’m in your debt!]

Bowing deeply, Subaru expressed his gratitude toward the girl―― toward Arakiya.

Although she probably did not hold a favorable impression of Subaru due to his treatment of Louis a moment ago, for his part, Subaru felt a strong sense of gratitude and debt toward Arakiya.

And the person who had ordered Arakiya to do this for him was――,

Subaru: [Thank you for saving us. Umm…]

???: [――Vincent Vollachia.]

Subaru: [――――]

Vincent: [Seventy-seventh Emperor of the Sacred Vollachian Empire, Vincent Vollachia.]

The one who introduced himself once again was the handsome man with black hair, sitting behind an ebony desk.

This person was the one who had confronted Subaru when he had snuck into the Imperial Residence and had come one step short of striking him down for his insolence. And, if the name he had just given was the truth, he was the most powerful man in the Empire.

Subaru: [Arakiya-chan?]

Arakiya: [It’s true… or a bit of a lie?]

Subaru: [A bit of a lie?]

Vincent: [Arakiya, do not talk out of turn. ――If you wish to regain what you truly desire, take care to conduct yourself in a manner that does not upset my good graces.]

Arakiya: […Nnh.]

Arakiya, who had responded to Subaru and his attempt at confirmation, was rebuked by that handsome man―― by Vincent, and she nodded with a look of slight discontent.

Arakiya lowered Rem and Louis onto a sofa for guests, and let them sleep. As for Subaru, he wanted to separate the two sleeping there as much as possible, but since he lacked the situation or the standing to make such a request, he simply clenched his fists tightly and endured it.

After all, this was the Sacred Vollachian Empire.

Subaru had spent a year learning the culture and general knowledge of this other world; and this was the neighboring nation of the Kingdom of Lugunica, which differed from it starting from the soil on up, the Imperial Capital where a figure of most august rank resided.

Vincent: [So? Lolimancer, explain it to me once more.]

Subaru: […Rather than that, could you please refer to me as Natsuki Subaru? As you can see, I don’t have the lovely, charming , pretty girl that makes me worthy of the title with me right now.]

Arakiya: [What about this child?]

Subaru: [She’s a girl who’s not lovely , nor charming , nor pretty .]

Subaru gave a curt response to Arakiya, who had inquired thus while pointing at Louis. Then, he turned his gaze back toward Vincent once again, and the Emperor closed one of his black eyes.

Vincent: [Speak, Natsuki Subaru.]

Subaru: […No matter how many times you ask, it won’t change much. We were at the tower of the Sage, in the far east of Lugunica. A lot happened at the tower, but I’ll leave that out… In the end, part of the Witch of Envy overflowed from the shrine near the Great Waterfall and swallowed us. Then, the next thing I knew, I was flung to the grounds of this castle…]

Arakiya: […Your story sounds like a lie. Are you lying?]

Subaru: [I get what I’m saying is totally suspicious, but on the other hand there is no reason for me to give you a story that is nothing but lies, so I’d like you to believe me…!]

He had thought he had laid out the facts, but Arakiya was rightly suspicious.

However, it was the person concerned, Subaru, who wanted an explanation of the situation. After finishing the battle with the Gluttonies at the Pleiades Watchtower, and then losing a companion he did not want to lose under the pretense of a Trial, and just as his frayed heart had begun to settle, this had occurred.

Subaru: [I’m sure Emilia-tan, Beako, and the others are quite worried right about now… Something like, “I can’t believe you, you ended up in the Empire somehow, and on the grounds of the castle of the Imperial Capital no less.”]

Vincent: [That you are a spy quite lacking in the skill of your excuses, contrary the skill of your infiltration, is currently the most likely explanation. If there is a point of note, it is that you identify yourself as Natsuki Subaru.]

Subaru: […It’s not a lie, I’m telling the truth, but was that really that significant to you?]

Vincent: [It is well known to the Empire that the Lolimancer is one of the Knights to a Candidate for the Royal Selection. The menaces of the Witch Cult and the Three Great Witchbeasts are not something that even Vollachia is isolated from.]

Subaru: [I see…]

Vincent: [A non-aggression pact was signed between the Empire and the Kingdom. I could insist that your mere presence here has shattered that agreement, however…]

Subaru: [No, that’s, well you know, I plead for your forgiveness.]

It would be terrible if Subaru carelessly giving out his name was the cause of the two nations plunging into a state of war. In the first place, this was truly an unfortunate misunderstanding, an unforeseen accident.

Subaru had no way to explain it, and it was shameful that he could do nothing but desperately insist that the truth that appeared to be a lie was, in fact, the truth, but――,

???: [My ohhh~ my, that’s just a bit too much of a threat, now isn’t it, Your Excellency? I don’t think we can afford to deal with the Kingdom right now, myself.]

Subaru: [――! W-who are you!?]

Subaru’s shoulders twitched at the unexpected voice of a third-party, and he turned around. When he did, he found that the office door had opened slightly, and his eyes met with the suspicious person peeking through the opening.

The suspicious person whom he had made eye contact with waved at Subaru, and opened the door with a defiant smile. Then, with broad strides, he brazenly stepped foot into the office.

Suspicious Man: [In accordance with my commandment, I have been called here, Your Excellency.]

Vincent: [I do not remember calling for you.]

Suspicious Man: [I didn’t saaay~ that, though? I said, in accordance with my commandment. I rarely get the chance to, so when the odd opportunity comes, I need to act as a proper Stargazer.]

The one who responded with a frivolous smile to Vincent, the Emperor, was a gentle-looking effeminate man with long ashen hair.

He seemed to have a different air about him than the soldiers he had seen in the castle, or the transcendental beings he had come across, and as far as Subaru could see, he did not seem to be a fighter.

Subaru: [Umm, this person is…]

Arakiya: [I hate him.]

Subaru: [I don’t want to know who you like or dislike, I want to know what his position is.]

Suspicious Man: [Ah, sorry, sorry. I’m not very attentive at times like these. My naaame~ is Ubilk, and I’m technically a Stargazer at this Crystal Palace. Pleased to make your acquaintance, Stargazer-san of the Kingdom.]

Subaru: [Stargazer… of the Kingdom?]

Subaru tilted his head at that unexpected sound when he was called such by that effeminate man―― the man who named himself as Ubilk, with a frivolous smile still on his face.

However, before Subaru could find out what that meant,

Vincent: [Natsuki Subaru is a Stargazer? Are you certain?]

Ubilk: [If you’re asking me if I’m certain or not, I have no way of confirming it since the Kingdom is outside my jurisdiction, but… I’d wager Your Excellency has come up with a similar theory regarding it.]

Vincent: [A puppet of the stars such as yourself would pose a conjecture as to my speculations?]

Ubilk: [Of course nooot~, I don’t have such a high view of myself as to believe myself capable of guessing the thoughts of Your Excellency, Emperor Vincent Vollachia… I’m just giving a recommendation.]

Vincent: [――. You may speak.]

Ubilk: [I have recited the stars. ――He will beee~ of great use to you, Your Excellency.]

Jerking his chin, Ubilk made that evaluation of Subaru in a light-hearted tone. In response, Subaru pointed at himself and instinctively said, “Me?” out loud.

Truthfully, combining this treatment as a Stargazer, the details of which was still unclear to him, with the discussion about Subaru, made him feel like this exchange being had was going over his head.

Ubilk: [Considering our relationship with the Kingdom, the intention to sever that anxiety of what may come could well give birth to a pretext that will not vanish. If that‘s the case, I believe it would be wise to add him to your hand instead. You have some perfectly convenient hostages, don’t youuu~? It’s a quick way for you both to reach an agreement, no?]

Subaru: [Convenient hostages… Wait, you’re not talking about Rem are you? No way!]

Ubilk: [Ha haah~ ha, you really are an honest person. If you had insisted that this young lady who accompanied you here wasn’t valuable as a hostage, things would have changed a bit.]

Subaru: [Guh, nnn…]

Ubilk: [Ooor~, would you like me to rephrase that just now? The young lady who accompanied him is worthless to Natsuki Subaru…]

Subaru: [Ha? Rem is so precious to me that I would sacrifice my life for her without regret.]

After he replied exactly like that, he witnessed Ubilk’s smile deepen, and Subaru brought his hand to his forehead as he completely fell for the trap.

That said, he could not lie here and say that Rem was worthless to him.

Subaru: [I’m not Otto. I really can’t say something I don’t mean.]

Otto: [I can’t agree with you calling strategy in a time of crisis proof of a bad character, though!]

Subaru sighed, an imaginary Otto shouting in the back of his mind. Dismissing it with a wave of his hand, Subaru looked toward Vincent.

Vincent placed a finger on the tip of his slender chin, and looked like he was examining Ubilk’s current proposal. Although, from the look on his face, Subaru could guess that he had already arrived at his answer.

And sure enough――,

Vincent: [――Natsuki Subaru, the situation you have been placed in is far from bright. Regardless of the veracity of your prior poor explanation, the fact remains that you have stepped foot into my country. And beyond that, this is while the Empire has entered wartime and is in the middle of an unparalleled national crisis.]

Subaru: [Wartime… There’s a war!? With who… where!?]

Vincent: [Here.]

Without censuring Subaru for panicking and forgetting to use respectful language, Vincent tapped the floor with his shoe. Subaru blinked, as he momentarily did not connect that response to his question.

But soon the implication reached his mind…

Subaru: [By here… No way, a civil war in the Empire?]

Vincent: [Precisely. The Emperor and the rebels shall fight over the throne of the Empire.]

Subaru: [――――]

At the confirmation of the reality of a war, a civil war at that, Subaru was involuntarily lost for words. Extending his hand toward that speechless Subaru, Vincent thus announced.

Like a bird of prey, with a gaze and expression of absolute power, the Vollachian Emperor thus announced.

Vincent: [No matter your circumstances, should you want to survive, you shall have to join me, Natsuki Subaru. ――In order to leave the Empire as it should be, in the hands of Vincent Vollachia.]

――Seriously, things had taken a troublesome turn.

Subaru: [――――]

Vincent Vollachia’s declaration caused Subaru to explode in rage with all his heart at the greatest absurdity of fate since he was first summoned to this world.

So far he had encountered many unreasonable situations. It could be said that he had been beaten down by countless absurdities, such as the hardship he had suffered at the Pleiades Watchtower.

And yet, there had still been continuity between them. It could also be said that there had been reasonable logic in how those situations had slowly gotten worse and worse, until it had been driven into an absurd situation.

Yet this time, it was not that way at all.

Subaru’s arrival in the Vollachian Empire, without any warning, had been absurd. If it had not been the Imperial Capital of Vollachia, but a more remote region, or perhaps the Kararagi City-States or the Holy Kingdom of Gusteko that he had been sent to, it would not have been so strange, and yet, it was here.

If he could not call this absurd, then just what could he call it――,

Arakiya: [Ah.]

???: [Uuh, nnn…]

Suddenly, Arakiya noticed something, and let out a sound, followed by Rem on the sofa beginning to stir.

Realizing this was a sign of her awakening, Subaru turned to look at Rem with a snap. Then he knelt next to her on the sofa and waited for her eyelids, framed by her lashes, to slowly open. He could vaguely see himself reflected in her pale blue eyes, and…

Subaru: [Rem! Thank goodness, are you okay? Do you hurt anywhere? Are you injured, or feeling sick? If anything is unusual anywhere, let’s immediately…]

Rem: [――Hk, why are you here!?]

Subaru: [Ghwow!]

After that brief period of him worrying about her condition, the awake Rem immediately shoved Subaru away. Subaru was blown away by the unrestrained power of that strike, and Ubilk lay in his trajectory.

With a “Huuuh~?”, a wide-eyed Ubilk was caught up by the flying Subaru, and the two of them tumbled to the edge of the room, entangled.

Ignoring Subaru and Ubilk, Rem sat up on the sofa and scanned her surroundings.

Rem: [W-where is that child… and you! From before!]

Arakiya: […Your Excellency?]

Vincent: [――. This is the Imperial Residence of the Emperor. This is far too noisy for such a place.]

Witnessing Arakiya before her, Rem became even more wary. Seeing Rem’s gaze, Arakiya turned her sleepy eyes toward Vincent, and the Emperor quietly lamented so.

As the Emperor had said, the situation was somehow lacking tension, and yet――,

Louis: [Uuu?]

The scene with the least tension was when Louis woke up late, rubbed her eyes, then tilted her head quizzically.

△▼△▼△▼△

――Trespassing upon the Imperial Residence inhabited by His Excellency Vincent Vollachia, located within the Crystal Palace at the northern end of the Imperial Capital Lupugana of the Sacred Vollachian Empire.

The crime committed by Subaru and Rem would definitely get them executed around seven times over.

Subaru and her were convicted criminals by Imperial law, but the reason they were not executed was due to the considerate discretion of the Emperor overflowing with mercy and compassion―― of course, that was not the case.

???: [As far as I am concerned, I would prefer to place individuals such as yourself that are inconvenient to deal with under house arrest until the issues of highest priority are dealt with, and remove the option of adding you to the discussion.]

Subaru: [You’re being super clear that I’m a nuisance, huh?]

???: [You are aware of this yourself, are you not? Under these circumstances, giving your name as that of a Knight involved in the Royal Selection of Lugunica, regardless of the veracity of that claim, only invites needless disaster.]

Subaru: […Unfortunately, my fame in the Kingdom is only around the level where passersbys on the street will wave at me.]

Having said that, Subaru was also starting to contemplate on whether it had been imprudent of him to have carelessly given his name. However, if he had done or said anything other than giving the name Natsuki Subaru at that time, he feared he may have left himself under Vincent’s discretion without any negotiation.

It had probably been the correct decision to confront Vincent in proportion to the willingness to listen he had displayed.

Subaru: [The others came to take my life without any questions…]

???: [If anything, I am impressed your neck is still so well connected to your body… The fact that you headed straight toward the Imperial Residence where His Excellency was at is also a point that adds to my suspicions.]

In that regard, it had been a process of elimination where every other route had been a beeline toward disaster, but it was clear that he would not be able to convince this old man with slits for eyes with such an explanation.

Imperial Prime Minister, Berstetz Fondalfon. ――That was the name and title of this old man with slits for eyes, and it was easy to understand the reasons why he was wary of Subaru, an outsider.

Subaru: [No matter what I say, you’ll think what you do, but I’m really not plotting or scheming anything. To be honest, I want to return to Lugunica soooon.]

Berstetz: [As you stated, it does not matter what you say to me. With the present state of affairs where border crossings are already restricted, it is unfeasible to be rash and send you back there when you have yet to be cleared of suspicions of being a covert agent.]

Subaru: [A torrent of sound arguments…]

Subaru sighed and his shoulders drooped at Berstetz’s strict words.

This place was a corner of the Imperial Capital, Lupugana, and it was here where Berstetz’s manor lay. Subaru had received a gracious verdict for his crime of trespassing upon the Imperial Residence, and he was being kept at the estate of the Prime Minister for now.

Berstetz, who was well-regarded by the Emperor, Vincent, was properly complying with the order to hold custody over his person, although he did not relax even one ounce of vigilance toward Subaru. Subaru too, had no major complaints about his treatment, despite feeling the sharpness of Berstetz’s attitude of unconcealed distrust.

If he had to say anything, it would be that it was almost frustrating that he had been so thoroughly strung along by Vincent’s calculations and had been unable to take any proactive steps to return to the Kingdom.

Or perhaps, the greatest reason Subaru and the others had been entrusted to Berstetz’s mansion, which had even stricter security than the Crystal Palace or the Imperial Residence, was due to that――,

???: [――I’m friggin’ back.]

En route back to his assigned room after finishing his interrogation by Berstetz, Subaru witnessed a flying dragon enveloped in a shroud of wind alighting in the garden of the mansion and a petite figure dismounting from its back.

The one there was a young girl in an adorable outfit, with two black horns that sprouted out of her sky-blue hair―― yet in contrast to that cuteness, she was a dragonkin who possessed unbelievable strength.

Subaru: [Madelyn-chan.]

Madelyn: […You friggin’ human. Don’t be so friggin’ casual and use “chan” for this dragon.]

The returning dragonkin girl, Madelyn, took notice of Subaru calling her name, and sniffed softly.

Madelyn seemed to be under Berstetz’s patronage, just like Subaru and the rest, and he often had the chance to cross paths with her in the mansion and interact. However, whenever they did, her bearing was harsh in this way, so he could not say they had established a good relationship.

Her harshness was not only directed at Subaru, but everyone at the mansion as well, however――,

Berstetz: [General First-Class Madelyn, how did it go? Those seeking the emancipation of General First-Class Goz are…]

Madelyn: [I friggin’ kicked them away. Let me say this now, us dragons don’t have any friggin’ obligation to take your insignificant circumstances into consideration, so I really did literally kick them the frig’ away.]

Berstetz: [No problem. His Excellency the Emperor ordered you to quell the revolt, and if you did what you deemed necessary to do so, then that is what is right for the Empire.]

Madelyn: [Hmph, you friggin’ boring senile fool.]

Madelyn shrugged at Berstetz’s answer, and upon her back she carried an armament around as large as her own petite frame―― a boomerang.

There was blood here and there upon the boomerang that she had failed to wipe off, and there was no doubt that was related to the “quelling” the two of them had discussed.

Subaru: [General First-Class Madelyn Eschart, and General First-Class Goz Ralfon…]

Murmuring that softly, Subaru thought of that which was beyond the walls that encircled the mansion―― of the landscape of the Imperial Capital with its buildings in orderly rows, and organized the various relationships swirling there through his head.

When he had first been sent here, he held almost no knowledge regarding the Vollachian Empire, and could only wander in confusion, but thanks to living in the mansion for the past few days, he now knew a few things.

For example, the one before him, Madelyn, had been bestowed with the rank of General First-Class, which was bestowed upon none but the strongest existences of the Empire, and

was a member of the Nine Divine Generals, an individual of the greatest military ability.

The other was also a member of the same Nine Divine Generals, a character known as the renowned Lion Knight, Goz Ralfon, who had rebelled against the Emperor, and was currently restrained within the prison of the Crystal Palace. The violent actions of Goz, who had a profound bond of trust with his subordinates, had caused much chaos amongst the troops.

It appeared that the group of soldiers Madelyn had just routed had been appealing for the pardon and release of the imprisoned Goz. He could understand saying that such a response was reasonable, since by siding with Goz, who had turned his blade against the Emperor, they too possessed the potential to become part of the rebels.

Subaru: [I’ve thought this day after day, but the culture is just too different…]

The Kingdom of Lugunica was about as safe and peaceful as modern-day Japan―― As someone who had lost their life many times in the Kingdom, this was not something Subaru would ever say. However, clearly different rules from the Kingdom had been imposed by the Vollachian Empire, and it was exceedingly difficult to ascertain the boundary between common sense and senselessness.
