※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※

――He had imagined that the time to pay off his accrued debts would have arrived more dramatically.

???: [――Heinkel Astrea-dono, there is an active order requiring your presence at the Royal Capital. You shall be coming with us.]

Informed as such by the Knights that surrounded him, all clad in the white garb of the Kingdom’s Royal Guard, Heinkel had been sitting in the corner of a tavern during the middle of the day, cheap booze in hand, anguishing over the gloominess of his future prospects.

Faced with the Knights who, aware of his identity, had called for his surrender, Heinkel felt genuine sympathy for them, seeing as how they were being forced to do a job they did not want to do.

Heinkel: [Royal Capital, the Royal Capital, huh… just what crime could they possibly be trying to arrest me for?]

Knight: [Unfortunately, we lack the authorization to inform you. Still, if you are going to resist…]

The air of tension amongst the knights rose palpably.

His exhales carried a thick scent of liquor, but the intoxication had yet to reach his head. Through the senses of his skin, Heinkel deduced that other than the three before his eyes, there was also a squadron of Knights waiting outside the tavern.

To make a long story short, they would not hesitate to use force. And, Heinkel did not possess the strength to force their senses of duty to yield.

Above all――,

Heinkel: [Even if I flee, it’s a stalemate, huh…]

It was not at all as though he had merely been gulping down cheap booze in despair. Before he ever filled his mouth with liquor, he had thoroughly wracked his mind in search of any means possible. After that, the reason he had headed to this tavern was because no matter how far he went, he had not wished to admit it. ――That he had already exhausted every possible option.

Heinkel: [――――]

Looking down at the cup still half filled with alcohol atop the bar counter, Heinkel bit his lip.

For the two objectives Heinkel needed to accomplish no matter what, there was a position he absolutely needed to acquire at any cost―― a position that would allow him to intervene in the Royal Selection.

Originally, his contact with Priscilla had been a coincidence, so it was purely by chance that he had been granted that position, but he had realized far too late that it was something he could not afford to lose. Hence, the best course of action Heinkel could take would be to seek employment at one of the two camps that remained after excluding the Crush Camp, where his father was involved, and the Felt Camp, where his son was involved.

Heinkel: [Emilia-sama’s camp is out of the question, and the Kararagi… Anastasia-sama’s camp would also probably be…]

Unfeasable; even Heinkel could comprehend that.

He would have liked to place hope in Anastasia’s reasonability as a merchant, but as he had learned in the Vollachian Empire, she was quite friendly with Emilia. In all likelihood, she would have already heard about the disgraceful display Heinkel had made in front of Emilia.

Even if not, Heinkel was also self-aware that his reputation was the absolute worst.

Ergo, Heinkel had no chance of being employed by any of the Royal Candidates.

And thus, that had been more than enough of a reason for him to have been completely crushed, the faint ray of hope he had begun to glimpse extinguished.

Knight: [Heinkel Astrea-dono. ――Your response.]

Pressed for a definitive answer amidst the mounting tension, Heinkel gulped down all the remaining booze in his cup, and lowered his hands.

Not once did he feel the mettle to attempt reaching for the beloved sword by his waist.

As they escorted him away, they did not even bother binding Heinkel’s arms as they stuffed him in a dragon carriage, somewhat anticlimactically.

He had been fully prepared for a more violent journey, such that they did not even treat him as human.

Heinkel: […In the end, what sort of pretext is this?]

Stuck between the Knights who, as always, would not answer him even if he asked, Heinkel pondered what crime of his was being called into question. ――There were many possibilities that came to mind.

He had completely abandoned both his obligations as Deputy Commander of the Royal Guard, and his position as lord of the Astrea domain; it was also completely possible that he was under suspicion of meddling in the domestic affairs of the Vollachian Empire. If it was about something more recent, there was also the fact that he had been about to assist in the scheme plotted by Aldebaran.

But then again, as he was the one who had been approached with the proposal, he wished to cry out, “This isn’t what we agreed on!” seeing as the plan had completely fallen apart before even a single thing could commence.

However, Heinkel did not have any intent of blaming Aldebaran for that.

Someone had attempted to accomplish something, and it had come to an end with them having failed to achieve it. If that were something to be blamed for, then even if Heinkel were to drown to death a hundred times in a sea of blame, it would still not be enough.

Once again, everything was back to square one.

That went for both dragging Reinhard down from the seat of Sword Saint, and awakening his wife who had been slumbering for nigh on twenty years.

Or, perhaps this was a good time.

With even his reason to keep struggling on taken away from him, perhaps this was a good time for him to be told to just give up already. If that were the case, he might have even laughed.

Heinkel: […Still, this is strange.]

Escorted all the way to the Royal Capital by the Knights who had assiduously refused to tell him anything over these few days, Heinkel furrowed his brow at the fact that he had not come out of the dragon carriage to the sight of the Royal Castle, a guard station, or even a prison.

What lay before his eyes was an old chapel constructed in a section of the Royal Capital―― belonging to the Church of the Divine Dragon, it was a building that Heinkel found difficult to face directly.

Speaking of the Church of the Divine Dragon, it was the state religion of the Kingdom of Lugunica, a bastion of prayer where many citizens, though varying in their piety, devote their faith toward the Divine Dragon, whose favor they all partake in.

In the past, Heinkel too had ventured there many a time to offer up prayers, wishing for the awakening of his slumbering wife. ――But, after that night, never did he return. He had no right to set foot there; at present, that was Heinkel’s self-evaluation in regards to the church.

In the Church of the Divine Dragon’s house of prayer, what awaited Heinkel as he was shoved along through the entrance, was a girl in a nun’s habit, with long golden hair, and ruby eyes――,

???: [Ah! I’ve been waiting for you, Heinkel-sama!]

The instant she saw Heinkel’s face, the girl clamorously flew out of her chair, quickly rushing toward him. At the momentum of the restless girl wearing a beaming smile, Heinkel reflexively took half a step back.

What he had sensed was not hostility. It was goodwill. The reason he had fallen back was not because of a threat. It was because of suspicion. The reason for that suspicion, upon eyeing the girl up and down once more, immediately connected.

Beautiful golden hair, and ruby eyes akin to blazing jewels.

Those traits ought to have been impossible.

Girl: [――I am Filóre Lugunica. I’m delighted to have the pleasure of meeting you like this, Heinkel-sama. I’ve been looking forward to your arrival!]

Heinkel: [ Fil… oh-re…!? ]

Filóre: [――? Yes, that is correct, Filóre. That is my… wait, that’s right! People who know it are always shocked when they hear it! Recently, everything all around me has gotten all busy and hectic, so I forgot to be careful about that.]

Sticking out her tongue to hide her embarrassment as she spoke, as the girl―― as the one who called herself Filóre faced him, Heinkel could not put into words the turbulence that had assailed him.

After all, it was impossible for there to be two people in this world who bore that name.

Filóre: [All of you, thank you very much for your assistance. For your wonderful work, the Dragon will also surely be delighted. “The arm of man doth swing the sword, but it be the Dragon’s will that deals in life. Under the footprints of a Knight chosen, even the most bloodied of ruts turn to roads of silver.” This too, is in the scriptures.]

Filóre called out to the Knights standing at the entrance to the chapel, behind the shaken Heinkel. At the sonorous reverberation of her voice, the Knights all exchanged glances.

Of course, from their perspective, having been the ones to drag Heinkel here, they would not want to do something like leaving Filóre and Heinkel alone here. But, without taking notice of the Knights’ concerns, Filóre declared “You need not fear!” with a clenched fist,

Filóre: [This personage is of the line of Sword Saints, the magnificent gentleman chosen by the Divine Dragon, I give him my personal stamp of approval! This is an extremely momentous encounter for the very Kingdom itself!]

As Filóre thud her own chest and talked bombastically, the Knights’ discomfiture did not fade.

On the other hand, Heinkel also had some vehement reservations about her remarks. It was to such an extent that it had managed to pull him back to reality from the initial shock of her name.

Knight: [If anything happens, please call out. We shall be on standby outside.]

Given their position, that was the limit on how much they were able to compromise.

And leaving those words behind, keeping a stern gaze on Heinkel until the very end, the Knights closed the entrance to the chapel, and took their posts outside. Once the sight of those Knights disappeared behind the doors, Filóre grumbled “How difficult” whilst folding her arms.

Filóre: [The situation is what it is, so it’s only natural that everyone is so worried, but… right now, this takes priority. Once again, Heinkel Astrea-sama, it is a pleasure to…]

Heinkel: [――Just before, what the hell were you trying to do?]

Filóre: [ Fweh ?]

Taking a step, he closed the distance of the half-step he had previously taken back, and questioned the other party. In doing so, as he looked down at Filóre from up close, her ruby eyes widened.

What discomforting eyes those were. In her refined facial features, he sensed far too many similarities to the Lugunican Royal Family. ――But, that could not be possible.

Heinkel: [Filóre Lugunica, is the princess who vanished from the castle fifteen years ago. And if it’s about her, she was already found in the slums quite a while ago, and now, in the Royal Selection…]

Filóre: [――Ah, you mean Felt, right? Indeed, I’ve heard that she also has those suspicions hanging over her. But, amongst ourselves, we have reached the conclusion that it doesn’t matter either way.]

Heinkel: [Ah…?]

Filóre: [It is possible that either she or myself is that princess who disappeared from the Royal Castle fifteen years ago. As it so happens, both of us are around fifteen years of age, and I believe there is a miraculous serendipity transpiring in that regard. However, that is unimportant.]

Heinkel: [J-just what sort of ridiculous nonsense are you on about!]

As Filóre brazenly touched so nonchalantly upon one of the foremost incidents of the Kingdom, Heinkel raised his voice.

In reality, it was ridiculous nonsense. Due to that terrible incident, there were several things that had ended up straying from the right path. And, it was not a matter unrelated to Heinkel either.

On that night fifteen years prior, the several occurrences that took place at the Royal Castle Lugunica――,

Heinkel: [That ties back to what you said earlier! That I’m of the line of Sword Saints, that I was chosen by the Dragon, spouting all sorts of nonsense…]

Filóre: [But, fifteen years ago, the one who basked in the Dragon’s Blood kept safe in the Royal Castle, never succumbing to the power it holds, before ultimately adapting to it… wasn’t it you, Heinkel-sama?]

Heinkel: [Wha――]

Filóre: [Ah, this was something that needs to be kept secret, right? To tell you the truth, it was something I stealthily read in the confidential records of the Church, so I only realized later that it was something that couldn’t be spread around.]

Though Filóre was belatedly trying to keep her voice hushed, Heinkel was in no state to care about that.

The Dragon’s Blood from fifteen years prior; the fact that it was even brought up in the first place was a shock, but the pièce de résistance was the fact that it was documented in something like the confidential records of the Church of the Divine Dragon.

The reason was lost on him. There was certainly a time when Heinkel had frequented the church, but it was not as though he was a devout adherent, nor had he ever done anything like confessing his inner heart to no avail.

Above all――,

Heinkel: [――――]

The suspicions raised against him, and the events of that night fifteen years ago: he would absolutely never reveal them.

The responsibility for the matter did not lie with Heinkel alone. It was an incident of grave importance that could well impact the rest of House Astrea, and the entirety of the Kingdom of Lugunica.

It was by no means a matter that would be put to rest if Heinkel alone were to lay bare his own heart.

Heinkel: [Hah, I’ve got absolutely no idea what you’re going on about, you damn phony princess.]

Thus, as Heinkel’s cheeks contorted with spinelessness, he attempted to viciously scorn Filóre.

Upon hearing it, Filóre widened her eyes, catching her breath at Heinkel’s denial. Did she really not consider that she might be denied? In that case, she was a foolish girl.

Heinkel: [Did you think that if you crashed into things head-first with honesty, everything would just neatly bounce back to you? If so, that’s an unthinkably carefree approach. The world isn’t such a nice place.]

Filóre: [Heinkel-sama…]

Heinkel: [Don’t go slapping on honorifics as if they’re some kinda uniform! I don’t know what you’re expecting from me, but it’s too bad. Chosen by the Divine Dragon? Don’t joke with me. The line of Sword Saints? Is that your aim? The Royal Castle and the Church of the Divine Dragon have always kept a distance! If you guys revere the Divine Dragon above all else, then Reinhard must be in your way, yeah!?]

Rapidly spitting out a string of foul speech, he felt the depths of his chest being tainted in viscous black.

He had just been half-mindedly vocalizing his thoughts, but surprisingly, he felt like the words he was saying rang true. The name of the Sword Saint was renowned in the Kingdom of Lugunica, and in the current age of Reinhard, celebrated as the strongest one in history, it could possibly be said that it was approaching the realm of religious faith.

It was possible that for the Church of the Divine Dragon, Reinhard was something like a thorn in their side.

In order to remove that, it was completely conceivable that they intended to use Heinkel. ――That which, until now, Heinkel himself had used as a card in his negotiations with the Royal Candidates, was now tinged with an unpleasant clamminess.

But, perchance, considering one of Heinkel’s objectives, that could also――,

Filóre: [――The reason I sought you out, Heinkel-sama, is because I wanted to have you become my Knight.]

――.

――――.

――――――――.

Heinkel: […What?]

Due to his deep rumination, in which he ground his teeth to the point where he could taste blood, he felt like he had heard an odd auditory illusion.

If not that, it must have been some inexplicable mishearing ; Heinkel grimaced with such sentiments, however, paying no mind to his bafflement, Filóre raised her visage, and opened her mouth.

Once again, this time staring directly into his azure eyes,

Filóre: [Heinkel Astrea-sama, I wish for you to become my Knight. With a delayed entry into the Royal Selection, the Knight of this very Filóre Lugunica.]

Heinkel: [Idi…! A-are you insane…!?]

Filóre: [My, what an awful thing to say! I’ll warn you now, but if you swear an oath to serve me, I’d like for you to reform that attitude as much as possible.]

Forcing him to swallow the fact that he did not mishear her, she doubled down on the sentiment. But, no matter how many times she repeated it, there was no way a proper discussion could take place with such an unsteady foundation.

Filóre had said it. That as a Royal Candidate, she would have Heinkel be her one and only Knight.

Heinkel: [Who do you have whispering in your ear? Don’t tell me, was it Reinhard? Did he say something to you? Then…]

Filóre: [Don’t make jokes! How could I thoughtlessly make such an important decision based on what someone else tells me to do? I came to this decision completely by myself!]

Heinkel: [If that’s the case then you’ve really got no eye for this sort of thing whatsoever! Didn’t you tell anyone else? For example, those Knights out there. There ought to have been plenty of people you could have asked!]

Filóre: [Yes, I did ask them. Everyone made complicated faces, and insisted that I should rethink it.]

Heinkel: [Then listen and do as you’re told! Rethink it!]

Filóre: [I did rethink it! But, no matter how many times I rethink it, you always end up as my number one choice, Heinkel-sama.]

Placing her hands on her hips, Filóre puffed out her chest and answered proudly, leaving Heinkel speechless.

She was likely the type to stick with something to the end once she had decided on it. Even just judging from her behavior until now, he generally understood that. He understood it, but what the hell were the people around her doing?

Heinkel: [Miss Priscilla also had a stubborn side to her, never budging once she’d set her mind on something, but in her case, nobody could deny her decisiveness and ability to get things done…]

In the sense of not lending an ear to the words of those around them, it might have been a close contest.

But, between Priscilla and Filóre, there was a great disparity in their individual reliability, or rather, in the degree of their strength of character.

To put it bluntly, Priscilla had been an adult, and Filóre was a child. If a child was attempting to do something wrong, it was an adult’s duty to stop them.

Even if that child bore a prestigious title such as Royal Candidate, and even if the adult in the position to admonish them was a foolish, wretched failure who had no right to do so.

Heinkel: [Even if you’re a dreamer, that which you’re dreaming of right now is a nightmare. It’s the kind of bad dream where you won’t even lend an ear to everyone around you telling you it’s a nightmare. How could I possibly go along with that?]

As he asserted that, Heinkel derided his own foolish decision.

Even though he had lost any Royal Candidate to rely on, and had been drowning himself in alcohol without being able to achieve his desires, now that this hand, the best thing he could possibly have hoped for, had been extended to him like this, he did not grasp it back.

If it had truly been so important to him, he ought to have reached out his hand by any means, fair or foul. ――In that case, after having spent fifteen years, could it be that he was not really serious about it, still trying to pick and choose the hands he took?

All of it was naught more than the mere dregs of convictions firmly rooted within him, with Heinkel’s interior being completely empty――,

???: [――You’re spoolio! Heinkel-san!]

That instant, a voice clearly resonated in a corner of his mind, quaking Heinkel’s very soul.

Heinkel: [――Louanna.]

For nearly twenty years now, he had not heard her voice even a single time.

Even so, whenever he closed his eyes, and pictured her smile, he would be able to hear her voice not only as if it were just yesterday, but as if she was right there with him in this very moment. It was only natural. He loved her, after all.

Even if Heinkel was completely empty, he had been filled with an ardor known as Louanna, along with everything she had given him, and all of that was real.

Not once, not even for a single second, had any of that ever faded.

Filóre: [I am appointed as a Saintess of the Church of the Divine Dragon. The ideal I espouse as a Royal Candidate, starting with erasure of the ill feelings between the Royal Castle and the Church, is the complete abolition of any factors that stand in the way of bestowing salvation.]

Before the silent Heinkel, Filóre started speaking quietly, but with a certain strength in her voice.

Raising his visage, Heinkel gazed at Filóre. As always, she was staring directly toward Heinkel, however, the words she weaved were bereft of the same frivolous atmosphere from earlier.

In order to impart the words she had to share with him no matter what, she was carefully selecting her words, imbuing them with strength and sentiment alike; that much was clear to him.

Filóre: [Heinkel-sama, I’ve heard about your wife. It would seem as though you have been searching for a way to awaken her for over a decade, not once ever giving up. It is extremely admirable.]

Heinkel: […You think it’s admirable? I’ve accomplished nothing. Louanna still isn’t awake, so what the hell is…]

Filóre: [No, it’s admirable! Nobody has ever commended you for it, have they? But, I think it’s incredible! It’s not something that just anybody can do. You’re indomitable… no, I’m sure there have been times when your spirit has been broken. Even so, the fact that you were able to stand back up is amazing!]

Heinkel: [――――]

Filóre: [That’s the kind of person you are, which is why I want you to be my Knight. Of course, as a Saintess, I also can’t overlook the fact that you were chosen by the Dragon. But, you are someone who does everything in your power without ever giving up for the people precious to you. I’m sure we’ll make a great match!]

Raising her voice, Filóre extended her smooth, white hand. And as if imploring Heinkel to take her hand, her ruby eyes blazed as if a flame was alight within them.

A foolish girl; no matter how much he heard of what she had to say, that impression did not disappear.

The individual whom a Royal Candidate selected to be their one and only Knight would become an existence who they entrusted not only with their own life, but with their political destiny as well. Even with a lofty title like Saintess of the Church of the Divine Dragon, it was all prone to being blown away by Heinkel’s notoriety.

There was not even a sliver of a reason for Filóre to choose Heinkel as her Knight.

He would refuse her. He should refuse her. Not for anyone’s sake, but for the sake of this foolish girl before his eyes.

In order to prevent this foolish and gentle girl from being ridiculed as an idiot, from being insulted by everyone behind her back, Heinkel ought to refuse her request.

And even though he ought to have refused her――,

Heinkel: [――Let me hear… one thing.]

Even though he ought to have sneered at her, turned his back, and walked away, he ended up speaking those words.

It was not a refusal. Neither was it a disparagement. As he expressed intent to continue the conversation, Filóre inclined her head.

Filóre: [What is it?]

Heinkel: [I’ve heard that the Church of the Divine Dragon has secret arts of healing that are forbidden from being revealed to the public. Maybe… just maybe, if such a thing truly exists, then…]

Filóre: [――You mean the Sacrament?]

Heinkel: [――Hk! Is there really such a thing!?]

Filóre seemed to have an idea of what he was talking about, and Heinkel pounced at her words. ――That vigor of his caused Filóre to widen her eyes, before she cast her eyes slightly downward.

While the change in her expression affirmed the existence of the sacrament, it also told Heinkel that she was uncertain if it would meet his expectations―― if it would be useful in awakening his slumbering wife.

Filóre: [――. There is. But, I don’t know whether it will have an effect on your wife or not.]

Sure enough, after a moment of silence, Filóre shook her head from side to side.

But, he did not get overly dejected. Having his hopes dashed, and being pushed down to the bottom of the cliff was an experience Heinkel was by no means a stranger to. The fact that he would not die even when that happened, was a result he had verified many times.

Heinkel: [I see. Is that so… Ahh, that’s right.]

He had already experienced more than enough shame in his life.

If his mind was wired in any respectable way, then even his question just now was something he should not have asked. And yet, he had asked it. Upon doing so, his hopes were thrown to the wayside.

So now――,

Filóre: [――That’s why, we have no choice but to test it out. They’re always telling me that I mustn’t use it too frequently, but if it’s for the sake of helping people, it should be fine.]

Heinkel: [――Ah?]

Filóre: [Ah, but, as I said just now, I’m not certain if it will work. The Sacrament isn’t all powerful, and it also depends on the state of that person’s soul… however, the Church of the Divine Dragon also has a lot of other things that aren’t known to the public, so if we don’t give up, it should be possible to open a path forward. Yes, surely.]

Firmly clenching the hand opposite to her extended one into a fist, Filóre once more insisted the same way she had initially.

The contents of her insistence caused Heinkel to blink his eyes, and let out a ragged breath.

Heinkel: [――――]

Filóre did not say that it would work.

Neither did she say to leave it to her, nor promise that she would definitely save her. ――Merely, she vowed to not give up.

For nearly twenty years, Heinkel had failed to be understood by anyone, being ridiculed as a fool time and time again; the things he had never abandoned despite all that, were now being affirmed as completely natural by the girl before his eyes.

He knew. ――He knew that everyone, even the very Heinkel reflected in the mirror, constantly thought somewhere in the back of their minds that it might actually be impossible.

Filóre: [Heinkel-sama, please lead the way. No, House Astrea is indeed quite famous, so I also have a rough idea of where it is, but I feel hesitant about barging into a household when no family members are home. Moreover, it’s also a little complicated between me and Felt…]

As if to say that things could not remain like this, Filóre halted in her tracks after gallantly striding forward. Looking back toward Heinkel after passing him, she called out to usher him to accompany her.

And, having turned around, Filóre’s eyes widened in shock. ――After all, before her eyes, Heinkel was kneeling down where he had stood, and was bowing his head.

Filóre: [Heinkel, sama…?]

Heinkel: [I apologize for my repeated acts of discourtesy. Miss Filóre.]

Before the surprised Filóre, Heinkel deliberately refined his speech, and spoke.

Were he to become the Knight of a Royal Candidate, he would be involved in the Royal Selection once more.

If it were a Saintess who could wield even the sacrament kept hidden by the Church of the Divine Dragon, it might be possible to awaken Louanna.

If there was a chance she was the princess who carried the blood of the Royal Family, then with the authority she held, it might even be possible to obtain the ancient knowledge slumbering in the Royal Castle, or even the Dragon’s Blood itself.

If he enumerated such calculations, he could come up with any number of reasons to kneel.

But, the number one reason for why Heinkel knelt here, was not any of those calculations.

――Do I really still want to pretend to be a Knight, me of all people?

Heinkel: [I would like to accept your proposal. ――Allow me to be your Knight, Miss Filóre.]

Filóre: [――――]

Heinkel: [You may end up regretting that you chose me, but…]

Filóre: [No, I won’t! Never!]

As Filóre smiled like a flower in bloom, Heinkel looked a bit daunted, before biting down on the interior of his cheek.

Still kneeling, he unsheathed the sword at his waist, laid it on the ground, and performed a respectful bow. ――The way he straightened his back, the angle at which he looked up at his lady, and his knightly etiquette of dedicating his blade, none of it had been erased by his twenty years of disgrace.

The ruins of a Knight who had once pledged fealty to the Royal Family, now, after all this time, decided to put those airs on once more.

It was ridiculous. Truly, it was utterly ridiculous.

While completely daubed in that humorless ridiculousness, Heinkel Astrea became the one and only Knight to the brand new Royal Candidate, Filóre Lugunica.

――And those were the events of the day upon which Saintess and Backstabber established a relationship of master and servant.

※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※

Otto Suwen thought to himself that, upon reflection, this was a far more troubling matter than he had expected.

The incident had started with a trivial lack of ink for the nib of his pen. While visiting downtown to buy some, a girl had grabbed the hem of his cloak.

Girl: [Where is mommy…?]

The girl pleaded with teary eyes―― she looked to be around ten years old, an age where it would not be wrong to call her a little girl rather than just a girl. Being caught by a child of such an age; he believed the phrase “it’s all over” was an apt description of such a situation.

Otto: [At the very least, if she were a little older things would be different…]

Judging things based on the other person’s age group might be a mistake, but at times such as this, what crossed his mind was the dreadfully calculated thought of “How might this action affect the Emilia Camp?”

If the rumor spread that Otto had not helped the little girl here, then it would be a massive blow to the camp. Appointed as the camp’s Internal Affairs Minister, Otto felt he could not take such a risk.

Otto: [I don’t remember ever wishing for such a position, though.]

A sigh leaked out with such a thought, but there had been no one around to listen to his complaint. If someone had heard him, he could picture familiar faces and voices he had become accustomed to saying things like, “Oi, oi, look at the situation and reflect on yourself, Otto!” or “If Otto-kun isn’t up for it, it can’t be helped, but… that child must be sad right now, and I think we are the only ones who can do something for her.” Otto let out another sigh.

Otto: [Just so you know, normally I would not be lending out my hand so indiscriminately like this.]

Saying that, he took the little girl by the hand and started walking.

Today, the city of Costuul was buzzing with activity, caught up without a doubt in the excitement of the upcoming festival.

The unfamiliar appearance of the little girl, who seemed unaccustomed to the area, was perhaps someone who had come here from outside the city due to the festival.

In that case, it is highly likely that the parent who came along with the little girl and got separated must be at a place that stands out―― perhaps waiting at a landmark, or calling out for her.

Otto: [Listen closely, okay? Please remember this. From now on, if you are treated kindly by a stranger, if I happen to be the first, then it’s thanks to the people who made me be someone who does this kinda thing, it’s not because I am like this.]

At his words, the little girl nodded repeatedly with teary eyes, an anxious expression still stricken on her face. Whether she truly understood his meaning or simply did not want to be abandoned by Otto standing before her, he could not tell.

Just that, whichever it was――,

Otto: [My friends would be glad that you were spared from a sad experience.]

Muttering so, Otto took the little girl’s hand and walked through the bustling cityscape, where it would be only natural for a girl her age to get lost.

To think that being called by such a shameful epithet as “Lolimancer” was supposed to be reserved for his friend alone; he had suddenly found himself caught in a most unreasonable and unexpected predicament.

Otto: [Good grief, it would be really troublesome if life got even harder for me at this rate.]

Muttering such things, Otto Suwen slowed his pace so the little girl would not fall behind, and continued on.

――It would still be a little while before Otto, who had been restrained by the little girl and her family making a grand commotion over their reunion, realized that he had forgotten to buy the ink for his pen nib.

〈Fin〉

※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※

――I heard a voice ripe with hatred.

――A sound which would not leave my ears.

――Words imbued with rage followed me.

――It was frightening, so frightening that I could not bear it.

――I was being crushed by the pressure of this noise which did not obscure its murderous intent.

――It gripped onto my soul, and would not let go.

――There was myself, and with the more I clung to my life, the more I would hurt others.

――First and foremost, I was sorry, so sorry, and yet I was still drowning.

※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※

――A neck, was being strangled by a great force.

Straddling them, a light body was pressing down on someone, disabling all movement.

Shoulders were being held down by both legs and knees, small in size, the body floundering underneath without freedom. Before their eyes, white arms covered in vermilion abrasions were pressing down on their neck. An out-of-place thought flashed, that it appeared like blossoming flowers,

―― Chokechoke , chokechoke , such was the great force with which someone’s neck was being throttled [1] .

???: “――――”

Right in front of their eyes, was a pair of pupils glowing with passion.

Endless fury and hollow despair stretched deep, deep in those large round eyes.

A blank thought that falling into those bottomless eyes, passed through their head.

???: “Ah, kah… Uh.”

―― Badumbadum , badumbadum , such were the sounds of their legs flailing wildly [2] .

That they were struggling in an effort to escape, was not the case.

Things such as thoughts to escape, had already disappeared long ago. So, the struggle of those legs were not an expression of a will to live, but merely a tantrum born of sheer physical suffering.

The brain was lacking oxygen, the mind had lost its will to live, but the body was still writhing in protest.

Everything was discordant, an unbalanced way of being such as that was unsightly.

Can’t I just die quietly? I want to just die quietly.

As peacefully as possible, like I’m simply going to sleep, that’d be the most enjoyable way to die for me.

Alas, such a wish was not to be. Far from being granted, their fate was really to be the complete opposite of that.

???: “Buh, kuh, kuh.”

With wide-open eyes bulging from their sockets, biting down hard and foaming at the mouth, with a body grown emancipated after only a few short days, it was in this state that they twisted and groaned like a wounded beast.

A fitting end, or so ought to be said.

A fitting fate, or so ought to be said.

What, why and how was it that they had come to be in this kind of situation?

???: “――What’s so funny?”

Suddenly, a voice was heard.

One unlike these animalistic groans, it was a cold yet clear voice.

The owner of those eyes laden with fury, their lips pressed thin as they squeezed their throat, looked up at the sound of the voice.

???: “――――”

Even when asked what was so funny, they were unable to find the answer.

There was nothing funny here, in the first place. There really was not, so why even ask?

The question was confusing. Some rude kind of nonsense, a riddle.

Even if someone forced them to reply, they would not have any answers. Yet despite that, the time waiting in silence still felt like lying on a bed of thorns.

How many times had they been flung around like this, by the force of some divine providence, so absurdly and unreasonably?

???: “――What’s so funny?”

There was nothing funny about it.

???: “Huu, he, hehe.”

Then, was it that the person asking was directing it towards the wrong party?

Or, was it that this person was enjoying this moment without even noticing it?

Were they enjoying the situation of having this woman mount them like she was on horseback strangling away at their neck?

If that was it, then it was detestable; their rational thoughts escaped.

Woman: “――What’s so funny?”

There was nothing amusing here. Even though there was nothing, this question would be projected repeatedly, over and over again.

Not even projecting. She was not that far away. It was not even projecting.

Close enough to feel each other’s breath, gazing up at the beautiful face of the girl opposite him, they were surrounded by her voice. Blanketed in it.

She had, without words, without hurtful abuse, shown clear hate in her voice.

Woman: “What’s so――”

Funny , and then.

The question seeking an answer was expected again, but suddenly faded away like mist.

Woman: “――Guh.”

Tilted, the face of the girl in front of them suddenly tilted to the left.

Like that, her leaning body could not rise back. Her posture collapsed, and that girl’s body crumpled onto the white snow. Of course, as the thin arm formerly wrapped around his neck had also come loose, their path to suffocation had ended halfway through.

???: “――Geh, ah.”

Coughing, the bitter taste of blood ascended their neck.

Collapsing lungs inflated before receding again, sending much-needed oxygen through their body in turn. That was also a reflex, from survival instinct. A proper human being would not just refuse to breathe and die.

Questions like whether that would be something a proper person would do or not, were something they did not wish to discuss, at this juncture.

???: “――――”

The feelings that had been present within their heart up to this moment, that of resigning oneself to death, now faded away. They had been replaced with a desire to live dubbed oxygen, an obsessive desire that could not be let go. Frantically, earnestly, they greedily coveted more to the point of looking pathetic.

While like that, ceaselessly filling his lungs with cold air on every breath, they had come to realize.

???: “――――”

Amidst the accumulating fluffy white snow, before him, lay a girl collapsed on her side.

Through the poor complexion of her face and lips, the woman’s unrealistic beauty was raised to even greater heights. With her faint breaths turning to white mist, an omen of her life withering, her violently glistening eyes made for a strong impression.

Looking carefully, it was a sight that did not seem well-fitted for the snow.

Her uniform revealed bare shoulders and thighs; the thickness of its cloth was wholly insufficient for warding off the cold. The neck, the ears, and other areas easily chilled were exposed to the wind, a painful sight to witness.

They were only the clothes she happened to be wearing―― although, it wasn’t just the woman, but themselves too, that were in the same condition.

???: “――――”

―― Clackclack , clackclack , such were the sounds of trembling mismatched teeth striking.

Whether it was the cold, or the strong melancholy in their heart that was the culprit, they did not know.

In this situation, rather than worrying about the anomaly of their body, instead they could not take their eyes off the girl in front of him.

Woman: “――Em.”

Even fallen over in the snow, with half her face buried in it, she still looked beautiful.

It seemed that unquenchable hate and fury was inflaming that slender body and keeping it alive. Covered in wounds to such an extent, it was a strange situation that the girl yet survived.

???: “――――”

Countless corpses were lying around them and the girl, in that pure-white snowscape.

Those beasts that consumed life, indulged in it, and destroyed the soul, before the wind of this girl had all turned to corpses. So, in this place, the survivors amounted to only two. Themselves and the girl, only two.

That, too, in a moment, could immediately become one, become zero.

???: “――――”

What is it , so the girl delicately mumbled as they slowly stood beside her.

The fingers on both their hands were numb due to the frost, having taken a dark-red coloration. With body temperature having dropped immensely, there was no feeling remaining in the cold fingers. Weak itching was the only evidence that the fingers were still attached to the their body.

Shaking about those fingers that could not be relied on, they lifted a stone as big as a human cranium.

Without any reason or purpose, it was only a stone that just happened to be there.

The fact that they had raised it secretly brought them much relief.

They compared the stone in their hand with the collapsed girl.

For a moment, that stone held by their fingers seemed to quite resemble the face of the collapsed woman.

They did not know if they were laughing. However, the look that was ultimately seared into their mind, was severe like that of a demon violently projecting onto them murderous intent and hostility, and nothing more.

As to shake that off, in both hands they lifted the rock skyward.

Gazing upwards at that action, the owner of those pink irises spoke with a faint, yet unquestionably clear voice,

Woman: “――I will definitely kill you.”

――The sound of something hitting something hard, in the snow-blanketed forest slowly, slowly echoed.

It echoed.

※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※

――That day, the mansion of Margrave Roswaal L. Mathers’ collapsed with a whimper.

Ironically enough, the first to notice the collapse was the woman who, more than anyone else, had desperately struggled to maintain the mansion. And because of that, her actions had been ruthless.

???: “――――”

At its genesis, she had received from the master of the house, from Roswaal, a great benefit.

So, hearing that the maid sisters who had taken care of the mansion no longer held their positions, knowing then that the owner had nobody to take care of him, she immediately rushed to that owner’s side.

The change in the appearance of the owner brought a most terrible pain to her chest.

Those two suspiciously glinting, brimming with confidence, differently-colored pupils; the eccentric and frank way of speech; the pale makeup of a clown that could be said to be the epitome of bad taste; the choice of fashion that appeared to be clawing at other people’s aesthetic sense; just about every light had disappeared from Roswaal.

After receiving such a reunion with him, the woman―― Frederica, clenched her fists tight.

Frederica: “It cannot end like this. For the sake of those girls, I will…”

Earnest in thought, she would guard that place of belonging.

Rather than thinking on whether something could be done, focusing on hope and wanting to do something, for that reason she had started to act.

To uplift the mansion once again she toiled, taking the hand of the girl who was collaborating without even knowing she would drag the master who had sunk into languor, in apathy, busily going around every day.

There was no time to stop and fret for Frederica.

Even though sometimes she would grow disheartened with her state of mind in that difficult situation, she always raised her head with fervor.

Were she to falter at any point, she would not be worthy to gaze upon the faces of those precious to her.

At some point, she had forgotten how to smile. At some point, she had forgotten to welcome night with a relaxed mind.

Even then, Frederica did her utmost to protect that which she loved, to surround the bubbles spreading away on the water’s surface with her arms so they would not escape. Even so――

Frederica: “――Ah.”

By the time Frederica finally realized, it was already too late for everything in the mansion.

White, the soles of her shoes frozen to the hallway, she lost sight of where her own self was.

The sight of the once-familiar mansion had become distinctly different from what she knew.

The carefully-cleaned corridor; the kitchen where she had cooked; where she had run ragged for those that needed her care; all that Frederica knew on a daily basis had, in front of her eyes, now become a clouded white world.

And as for who had done all this――

Frederica: “Great Spirit-sama…”

???: “Sorry, Frederica. You’re not to blame―― it’s just that, if I’m to protect my most precious thing, then this is the best decision to make.”

Saying this, showing its face and floating in the air, was a small cat with gray fur.

Its size only that of a fist, yet a supernatural existence carrying immense power in that small of a body―― it was the Great Spirit, Puck.

She did not want to believe. But now there was no reason to doubt.

That was the one who had wrapped the mansion in this white demise, transforming it.

Frederica: “Why, do this…”

Puck: “I said it already, all my actions are for Lia―― Lia agreed to leave the forest because it was what she wanted to do, and also for her safety. Or so I thought. But there’s no worth here anymore. I wonder where it all went wrong.”

Frederica: “――――”

Puck: “Roswaal was my miscalculation. That pitiful thing’s just your everyday guy.”

Shaking their head, Puck shot at her with voice devoid of any emotion.

At those words, Frederica’s breath hitched. And soon afterwards, clacking her sharp denture,

Frederica: “――Insulting the master of this house in front of me, a maid, cannot be forgiven.”

Puck: “You, too, are a pitiful child. Only you are desperate to protect this fallen place.”

Frederica: “Please stop talking as if you are referring to the past, it is not over yet.”

She called sharply. Without having a chance, towards the Great Spirit.

Faced with Frederica’s words of defiance, the kitten narrowed their round eyes and gazed with pity on their face. Reacting to that existence’s movement and expression, which to some extent smelled human-like, Frederica leaned forward and lowered her body.

Frederica: “Emilia-sama would be sad.”

That one brief hesitation from the small Great Spirit might give her the win, this was what Frederica was hoping. But――

Puck: “Unfortunately, I’m weak to Lia. I cannot move on from my child, I’m a momma bear [3] .”

Even a moment’s hesitation, some small opening, from that Great Spirit did not appear.

As the world of difference between her and Puck reflected in her eyes, Frederica firmly smashed her molars together.

Whether it was the beginnings of regret or grief, it was too late to be felt.

Just a simple white breeze blew, and with that alone the woman named Frederica was frozen.

That marked the beginning of the collapse of Roswaal’s mansion.

By the time the warlock [4] noticed the signs of collapse, it was all already too late.

???: “――――”

With ghostly footsteps the warlock in their own mansion walked.

The frozen mass of air underfoot broke with a clatter, and a chill breeze tickled their nape.

His neck drew away from it, and immediately, an odd physiological reaction to that unpleasant cold was felt.

Nowadays, applying makeup to his face and choosing clothing had both been left to Frederica.

That diligent and enthusiastic girl was, no matter how, trying to pay back the grace she had received from this place, but it was too late. His heart that should not have have felt anything ached a little.

――The path to Roswaal’s dearest wish had, at some point, been severed.

Roswaal: “Ram, Rem…”

Maybe it had been triggered by the loss of the oni sisters.

The existence of those two was a key part in the path towards Roswaal’s utmost wish. With them having vanished, Roswaal had been left alone.

Four-hundred years later, upon realizing the road to his long-held hope had been broken, Roswaal could no longer stand on his own.

Roswaal: “――Ram.”

A short, mumbled name, it was the name that conveyed the biggest regret.

――The possibility that it would become like this, he had already considered it previously.

Quite the opposite, the likelihood that it would end badly like this was much higher. It was because of this that Roswaal had taken insurance on his own existence.

When his end finally arrived, he wanted someone there that could receive it happily.

Her, dying before him, had ruined the last remaining cogwheel in his plans.

Roswaal: “――――”

So then, it was strange for Roswaal, to find himself wandering through the frozen mansion.

He had lost his reason to stand already, and his reason for walking was already gone from him.

Frederica: “Master, please return yourself to how you were before. So the two of them――”

Many times, Frederica had so appealed to Roswaal.

With Roswaal falling into despair, his spirit weakened, Frederica had taken up the task of patiently and devotedly uplifting her apathetic master.

Henceforth, the power to walk in this now-frozen mansion remained in him.

Henceforth, in the middle of the hallway he was wandering in aimlessly, his sight now turned to the scenery beyond the window.

Henceforth, he saw that frozen world of white, and the form of the blonde-haired girl attempting to resist it.

Roswaal: “――――”

He perhaps thought, that to not protect her here would not do.

Or it could simply be acting on reflex, he did not know.

Enough remained of his mind in the body for him to decide on reflex that he must do so.

So now, Roswaal slowly spread his arms wide, readying himself to pour out a vast amount of Mana――

Roswaal: “――Kh!”

At that moment, Roswaal barely avoided the bright flash of a blade targeting his neck.

???: “――Oh my, to be able to dodge this is outside of my expectations. Perhaps the Head Magician of the Court isn’t only skilled in magic, but is someone holding some level of skill in martial arts as well?”

From behind Roswaal’s back called out a light voice.

His zori [5] attaining speed that could scorch the frozen corridor as they glided through it, it was the voice of a young man sporting dark-blue hair.

Blue-Haired Man: “That movement just now, it wasn’t something someone can just do on the fly. I’m honestly impressed.”

That terribly out-of-place person was clad in a blue kimono , wearing zori on his feet, and had two swords strapped to his waist. One of those had been unsheathed, and he was now tapping his shoulder with it.

A face with a neat appearance, donning a well-fitting smile. The bright eyes that gave a striking impression of a young mischievous child, and the long hair tied up both somehow offered him an androgynous look.

But from him emanated an aberrant yet transparent fighting aura―― just by being bathed in that ghastly gaze, visions of myriad deaths from a sword surface, so that anyone would be rendered unable to make rational comments.

The young man fluently spoke as he scratched his head with a shy smile.

While looking at this scene, Roswaal reignited his sluggish thoughts to stir again, as to solve the situation he had found himself in.

What played a part in that blaze, was the burning sensation at his left arm.

Roswaal: “――――”

Roswaal: “Your advice, I’m grateful for it.”

With that argument made by the young lad, Roswaal loosened his lips lost of the color of blood.

That Roswaal’s left arm had been amputated near the shoulder, and what had used to be attached there was almost unrealistically rolling on the floor, like the limb of a doll.

Alongside the first strike to his neck that had been dodged, his arm had been lopped off.

After hearing this advice to act, Roswaal grasped his wound, and an instant burst of fire directly stopped the bleeding. Horrible pangs of pain tore through his brain, but with rigid cheeks he bore it.

At that his extreme emergency treatment, the young man’s eyes widened ever so slightly.

At Roswaal’s low voice, the young man―― Cecilus Segmunt responded with an elegant bow.

There was no reason to hide his identity. There was no reason to hide his name in the first place, so he may as well act coolly dignified and confident.

Watching those mannerly ways with their dramatic productions, Roswaal sighed.

Roswaal: “But that aside, what’s happening now, I wooonder~? Ahh, it couldn’t be, at this time when the new Monarch of the Kingdom of Lugunica is being decided, the Vollachian Empire is moving in violation of the treaty?”

Cecilus: “Oh, that’s a misunderstanding. Right now you could say I am on break from being part of the Nine Divine Generals, or you could say I am unemployed. Anyway, this business has nothing to do with the Empire, now I am professed as the strongest ordinary… vagrant swordsman.”

Cecilus: “This is no poor joke. My actions, the Empire’s not involved in them at all. Of course, loyalty to His Excellency still lies in my heart… But, I got my reasons for doing what I do.”

With a grand gesture, Cecilus emphasized that he and the Empire were not working together. It was difficult to believe it unconditionally, it was fact the plans of the Empire were incomprehensible.

For this reason, Roswaal narrowed both his dual-colored eyes, and inquired of Cecilus,

Roswaal: “Then it’s even more curious. That you’ve even abandoned your position of General at the Empire, and come here. What exactly is it that can move you to such an extent, I wooonder~?”

Cecilus: “It’s easy to understand―― A step in the path towards the Heavenly Sword, was promised.”

Roswaal: “Path towards the Heavenly Sword?”

At that reply, Roswaal frowned his handsome brows.

Cecilus, witnessing that, nodded deeply in reply, and a murmur, “Yes”. The expression was just as if he was smiling, but a crucial difference lay in the emotion of the pupils.

With human emotions like that of joy and pleasure, the Blue Lightning severed human lives.

However, what lurked in the eyes of Vollachia’s strongest at this instance was not joy and pleasure, but a deeper hue, a more fervent hue――

Cecilus: “It’s a most important wish I’ve never spoken of to any living person. Someone guessed it correctly, and went on to say they could assist with it… There wasn’t any choice but to accept that opportunity.”

I accept the role of this world’s star actor, the leading part on its script. Beyond that, it’s part of an actor’s skillset to ad-lib lines and performances, isn’t it so?”

Cecilus shrugged, the emotions in his eyes returning to their previous state, and Roswaal simply nodded.

Indeed, at the strength of his argument, he gave up fighting against it. “Might makes right”, was the philosophy Cecilus had built over many victories.

To forcefully bend that notion was impossible for Roswaal, who had lived four-hundred years for an obsession of his own.

For Roswaal, who preferred stagnation, that philosophy seemed attractive to him, too.

Seemingly acting in his own breed of politeness, Cecilus returned the sword he held to its sheath. And with the sound of another blade being drawn, the blade of a beautiful sword was revealed to the world.

The beauty of the sword was truly arcane, a magic sword imbued with uncanny power――

Cecilus: “――Ranked highest among blades, the Dream Sword, Masayume.”

With the overflowing dreadfulness in front of him, Roswaal with a carefree tone raised a finger.

One-armed and bloodied, faced with a swordsman without peer in all epochs amongst the congealed atmosphere; yet in such a situation he raised a query towards Cecilus. The latter again tilted his head, at that out-of-place light-hearted tone.

Cecilus: “What are my weaknesses? My weak points are that I don’t listen to people and I don’t really have the composure of someone over twenty years of age. Oftentimes, that’d end up in the agenda of the Imperial Parliament.”

Roswaal: “Your employer’s name is?”

After that question was posed, Cecilus’s eyebrows raised slightly.

He lowered the blade while drawing a foot back. Slowly, he leaned his upper body forward,

Cecilus: “Gossip around has them down as a wretch, a fiend, and I’ve even heard some speaking ill in their back, calling them the Purge King… But to you, because I’ve been asked to communicate the correct name to you…”

With that as the preface, Cecilus wet his lips with his tongue.

After a dramatic pause, he revealed.

Cecilus: “――――”

With that name as an expression of power reaching his ears, Cecilus disappeared, cracking the floor of the mansion.

That he had vanished from the world, it was fast enough to mistake for that.

On that moment, the moniker of Blue Lightning truly befitted the man approaching like a bolt of electricity.

The distance was crossed instantaneously.

However, at that same instant, Roswaal weakly parted his lips, muttering,

Roswaal: “So it was you, after all.”

Even before the sound of those words appeared in the world, the Dream Sword drew an arc.

Just before everything went dark, Roswaal’s consciousness thought.

About those girls currently at the mansion, and their safety.

About those girls who had been become collateral damage in the path to his dearest wish, and had ultimately been left with no happiness at all.

――He did not possess neither the qualifications nor the time to apologize in those final moments, and so anything and everything vanished.

Door Crossing’s mechanism was a simple one, which functioned by connecting the entrance to the Forbidden Library to another doorway.

Due to that straightforward effect, the versatility of Door Crossing was quite high, and she was proud of this outstanding magic. But just like any other magic, Door Crossing was not wholly flawless as well.

If its method were revealed that useful nature could turn into weakness. Because of this, the existence of the Forbidden Library and the effect of Door Crossing had to be kept hidden from outsiders.

Indeed, outsiders were not supposed to find out about it.

――Henceforth, such a situation was inevitable, she thought.

Beatrice: “What irony, I suppose.”

At the moment the door to the Forbidden Library’s was touched, Beatrice herself already understood that they would be let inside.

That spacious mansion with its countless doors to choose from existed, and yet, Beatrice had forcibly been guided to a single one.

That method was simple―― a situation where the other doors could not open would do the trick.

The method to halt Door Crossing was to remove any choice of doors to connect to.

That task had been carried out with diligence, and so the doors that could be opened in the mansion had now been limited to one. And that who had helped in discovering this method must have been her dear brother, she somewhat understood.

Being put off-balance by this realization was inevitable. Because that was a common law for both their existences――

But even taking that into account, begrudging her dear brother was not fitting for her. Because of this, Beatrice, without holding any sort of resentment for her brother, instead quietly faced the door that had been opened.

???: “――Yo, Beatrice.”

That voice and attitude, she remembered it. Because of this, Beatrice’s body shivered with fear.

The face from her memories, and the face now seen in front of her, not every detail seemed to match up.

While it was in concordance with the general parts of her memory, they were already almost like another person.

Beatrice: “You, why are you giving me that look, in fact?”

Far from improving, it had changed in a way that drew even more revulsion.

That rare-to-find black hair and black eyes remained, yet the hair had lost its luster, while in those eyes that had lost their shine darkened emotions were dimly revealed.

Surrounding those eyes reminiscent of gloom were deep dark circles, thin and frail cheeks lay underneath, and what could be seen of the fingers displayed a corpse-like pallor.

With long dark clothes wrapping their body, exposure of the skin minimized―― among that united uniform of black, what stuck out was a bright orange scarf. Just that, and that alone, was quite strongly betraying their gloomy impression.

Some years had passed.

But despite that, too much had changed. How could a human become so different?

Beatrice: “You, your mood has seriously changed, I suppose.”

Human: “Same goes for you, then. Is your growth spurt over? Normally, you’d become a little more mature after two years have passed.”

In a blank voice, to Beatrice’s words they replied with a joke.

Two years, was it? If that person said so, then certainly that would be the amount of time that had gone by.

Just two years, from Beatrice’s perspective, was like the blink of an eye. To humans, especially to the one standing now in her sight, how meaningful would those years be, she wondered.

――Was that stretch of time so meaningful for that boy, who had been near death, to return for revenge like this?

At the words of that human, Beatrice crinkled her brows.

Once more, a large teardrop, flowing over that girl’s reddened cheeks, fell.

???: “There’s a proverb where I used to live, something like, a drowning man will even clutch at straws.”

Facing down towards the floor’s red carpet, a man was listening to the voice.

That carpet, his face was very close to it.

He looked to be reaching sixty, an old man.

Not just his son, but his grandchildren too had grown up, he showed the marks of having lived a long and fitting life.

That he was out of the ordinary, he did not have any thoughts of bragging like that. But having been born with a wit beyond the norm, he had resolved to live a life of abundance.

And that was why, in his current situation, he could not help but wonder whether he was in a dream or in an illusion. He could not believe it.

Purge King: “――――”
